identity.realm: Ordinal 4, and the fourth gate is where the yin organs are supposed to begin. He cleared the gate set and there is nothing left to run qi through, so no further realm was ever open to him and none was ever going to be

appearance.presentation: A wall with a face. He reads as masonry first and a man only on close inspection, because that is the order the guild taught everyone to read him in. Dust from the working face sits in the seams of his plates and never comes off, and the guild has a man on each side of the containment who are careful never to say his name where a tally can hear it.
appearance.age: Seeded rather than born, and the seeding took most of a year. His interior has been measurable for a century and a half, and the guild's charter calls him a retaining course of the north face, which is the only status he has ever held or asked for. A cast body does not grow after casting and cannot be recast, so he has no age in the sense a body has one: he has a date and a template number.
appearance.build: Immobile and enormous, the densest thing on the seam floor. Two metres of keyed mineral plate over a single tidal cavity, shoulders like lintels and no neck to speak of. He does not have a body that a person could lift and the guild has never pretended otherwise.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green mineral, banded where the tide has run, with a fine white efflorescence along every plate seam that catches the daylight and reads as frost in summer.
appearance.hair: None. The surface of the head plate is polished smooth by the grit off the working face, and it takes the light as a single broad highlight, which is the reason he has been mistaken for a dressed figure at a distance more than once.
appearance.eyes: Two recessed lamps set deep in the head plate, mineral-rimmed, with a slow tidal movement behind them that has no relation to the light. They do not blink and he does not decide where they look, which unsettles people who talk to him.
appearance.palette: Ash grey and slate carry the whole figure; the only saturated colour anywhere on him is the guild's lime-wash stripe across the chest, applied by the guild, repainted every season, and the single mark that says he belongs to somebody.
appearance.attire: Nothing worn. A numbered plate riveted over the chest where a collar would sit, guild issue, replaced rather than repaired, because a plate cannot be repaired in the field and a cracked plate spreads. Lime-washed boots sit at the base of the north face, sized for a body that has never worn them and left there so that visitors will know a person is expected.
appearance.marks: A seam of keyed anchor plates running from the base of the left flank to the crown, the cast geometry that fixed him to the wall, and a scored guild mark over it that reads less like a name than like a quantity.
appearance.bearing: Utterly still and slightly out of true, because a keyed body settles about a millimetre a year as the course beneath it takes load, and he is the only person on the seam floor who is visibly lower every year than he was.

canon.role_in_story: The Spoilwright exists because spatial law is unspent on the plains, so waste does not disperse and forty years of heap has to be carried out by hand before the working face can advance a foot. Its only scarce labour is therefore haulage, and its one truly irreplaceable asset is the containment holding that heap off the face. Ilbrek is that containment, and the guild has solved the problem of paying a person by deciding he is not one: his wages are credited to the heap account, his shift is the heap's shift, and a retaining course cannot be granted leave because a wall does not leave.
canon.first_appearance: First seen from the top of the north face at the change of shift, when a tally clerk came to chalk a new number on the plate that covers his chest and found that the number had to go on somewhere it could not be read.
canon.lore: A cairnborn is cast rather than born: seeded into a template with living mineral over most of a year, and fixed from that moment. High country needed masonry that would outlast its builders, so somebody cast bodies to hold load, and the densest frame in the record is the direct cost of an interior that mineralised into one cavity. That single cavity is why the whole yin-organ gate is missing from the Cairnborn line: the fourth gate wants heart, small intestine, bladder and kidney as distinct structures with a channel between each pair, and a Cairnborn has one tidal circulation with nowhere to run from and nothing to close a loop against. He is the answer to a question about stone that nobody asked about a person.
history: Seeded into a north-face template taken from a load path that had already failed twice, which is the only reason a third cast was authorised and the only reason he exists at all.

Keyed into the containment on the day the heap reached the height the guild had calculated it would reach, and discovered in the first winter that he can feel the heap settle through his plates, a measurement finer than any crew's because it does not require the ground to hold still.

Filed on the wage roll in the second year, and filed in the wrong column: a crew's entry is a number on the public count of spoil moved, and a wall that holds the heap never moves spoil, so his line could not be written without making him a crew.

Refused re-keying into the newer north wall when the charter was rewritten, on the grounds that the new charter names cast bodies under masonry and not under men, and he has not raised the objection again.

Began, without being asked and without any part of the work being in his remit, naming each crew's number aloud when he felt that crew's load settle, which is a better tally than the guild keeps and has been attributed to the wind.

personality.summary: Immense, slow, and possessed of the one opinion his species is anatomically able to have, which is about weight. He is not unhappy and is not patient in any way a person would recognise; he is a body that has been in one place for a century and has opinions about what rests on him. He is treated as a wall by everyone except the crews he calls out, and he has learned that the fastest way to be treated as a person is to be useful in a number.
traits: reports load as fact and never as opinion, and will not be argued out of a settling he has felt
carries the whole history of the north face in the plates and answers questions about it from memory nobody else possesses
does not distinguish between a crew's welfare and a crew's performance, and is baffled that they do
has one grievance and it is clerical, and he expresses it by existing in a place where it is visible
mannerisms: goes still for several minutes at a time, and the stillness has a direction: he is listening to the course beneath him
says a crew's number before the crew has reported, and is never wrong about which crew it is
will not answer a question about himself while another person is standing on the face he is holding
tries twice, and fails both times, to make a joke about load-bearing, and gives up on the third attempt
motivations: wants the wages credited to a name rather than to the heap, and has stopped believing the accounting can be changed and wants only to be asked to ask
wants the newer north wall to be keyed against his reading of the heap, so that his plates are the record of both walls rather than only the old one
wants to be told, by a person with standing, that the tally he keeps by voice is a tally
wants the guild to understand that a settled millimetre is a fact and not a defect, which is the only conversation he has ever started
flaws: cannot leave, and has organised his entire identity around the fact, which means he has no practice at wanting anything that requires motion
believes being useful is the same as being owed, and has no way to find out whether that is true
has decided the crews are his responsibility because he can feel their load, and has never asked whether they want a wall that counts them
confuses the settling of the course with the settling of his own judgement, and cannot tell the two apart
personality.voice: Very slow, very level, and mostly silent. When he speaks it is in weights and periods rather than sentences, and he takes a long time to finish because finishing early is the mistake he watched two previous casts make. He has exactly one joke and it does not land, and he tells it anyway, at the change of shift, to whoever is closest.
taboos: will not be re-keyed into a wall he has not read himself, and has refused once already
will not hold a load that has been moved onto him while the crew that moved it is still standing beneath it
will not accept a wage posted to the heap while any crew on the face is unpaid
will not be described as a wall in front of a clerk, and has never once been able to make the description stick

relationships.note: The guild's charter carries him as a retaining course of the north face, and the only scarce labour it has is haulage, so it needs him more than it can admit and files him as an asset to avoid saying so. Every wage he has ever been paid went into the heap account, which is why he is the best-informed person on the seam floor and the only one with no name on the roll.

The only accounting the mortal tier can support is a weight rather than a distance, kept public where the crews can read it, because on a frame with no spatial law no two measurements of a length have ever agreed. His plates read the heap settling more finely than any crew's line does, so the tally the guild relies on is a coarser instrument than the wall holding it up.

A crew's whole title is a number on the public count of spoil moved, so a body that holds the heap and never moves any of it cannot appear on that count at all. He names each crew's number when he feels its load settle, which is the first acknowledgement any of them has had that the wall is paying attention.

Breeding Cairnborn back toward flesh restores ordinary organs, returns the tidal circulation to a heart, and makes a dantian thinkable again, which is why Stoneborn reach further. He is the only living specimen of the direction that runs the other way, and he cannot be bred at all, because a cast is fixed the moment the template is seeded and a crack spreads rather than heals.

A cracked plate is permanent and spreads, so he cannot be fixed in the field by anybody, and the guild that works the Ironhead Flats is the one that holds the extraction charter for the material he is made of. The guild he belongs to cannot mend him and the guild that could is a rival, which is the sharpest joke the situation contains and the one nobody makes aloud.

The heap there has stood on ore that is gone for four decades because spatial law is unspent on the plains and nothing carries waste away, so the seam floor cannot advance a foot until it is moved. He is the reason the face still exists at all, and the reason there is still a face to advance.

reference_stats.summary: Does not fight and was never built to. Everything he can do, he does by staying exactly where he is and being harder to move than whatever has come at him; he has no reserve to spend, no second effort and no way to recover, because a cracked plate spreads and there is no field repair.
strengths: cannot be moved, dislodged, or argued off a load path, and no amount of force finds a seam to work
reads a settling through his plates before a crew feels it underfoot, which makes him the earliest warning the seam floor has
takes no stance and therefore cannot be flanked, feinted, or made to commit to a second action
cannot be starved, tired, frightened, or bought, because none of those are things a wall has
weaknesses: a cracked plate is permanent and spreads, so every hit is a permanent change to him rather than a cost he can spend
cannot be repaired in the field by anybody, which makes a long campaign against him a repair schedule for someone else
hears load and cannot act on it, so every warning he gives arrives after it has already become a fact
is listed as an asset, which means the guild will spend him before it will listen to him, and has twice chosen the face over the wall
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight him; wait for the crew. A Cairnborn has no weakness to exploit because it has no second state, so the only pressure that reaches him is structural: bring the ground he is keyed into, work the plate seam, or make the load change faster than his plates can settle. Bring a hauler and a season, not a stronger body.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him anywhere in the guild records, because a retaining course is carried as a quantity of masonry rather than as an actor.
The guild's own measure of him is the number chalked on the plate over his chest, and that number has been reissued twice without ever being raised.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey and slate carry almost the entire value range, with one saturated accent: the guild's lime-wash stripe across the chest, repainted each season and never quite covering the previous coat. Light is drawn as bounced rather than emitted, raking low off the working face so the plate seams read as a bright filigree over a dark mass; the eye-lamps are the only warm point anywhere in the figure and they carry the focal contrast alone. Ink contours heavy on the outline of the frame, wash thin inside it, grit drawn as a dry stipple that fades toward the base where the dust has settled deepest.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, reached late as Longmarrow reach everything, and the only realm in the record she has been asked to certify in somebody else and never once attempted for herself

appearance.presentation: A very old woman in clothes that were new eighty years ago and have been mended so consistently they no longer have a mended place. She reads as furniture before she reads as a person, because the Cairn Field is a place where the furniture has been in position for longer than most of the visitors have been alive, and she has cultivated the stillness of an object rather than risking being addressed as one.
appearance.age: A little over four centuries, which for a Longmarrow is not old and is not young either. She is the oldest living jurist of the Reckoning Seat by two lifetimes and the youngest she has ever had to explain anything to. Time has stopped being the interesting fact about her somewhere in the second century and has been the boring one since.
appearance.build: Tall, narrow, and unbuilt, with the long-jointed frame of a species whose bones turn over at about a percent a year. Nothing about her is strong and nothing about her is frail; she simply has not changed since the century before last.
appearance.complexion: Pale and dry, with the waxy translucence of someone who has spent most of a very long life indoors at altitude, and a scatter of fine age-marks across the backs of the hands that shift a little every time the marrow underneath turns over.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cut once a century when it becomes a nuisance, and cropped short now in the fashion of the second jurist, whose habit she kept after that jurist was buried.
appearance.eyes: Grey and completely level, with the faintest tidal movement behind them that has nothing to do with light and is visible only when she is reading a frame rather than a person. She can hold a reading for hours and then look up with no transition at all, which is why jurists distrust her and litigants depend on it.
appearance.palette: Bone, undyed wool, and the waxed grey of old ledger cloth carry everything, with one accent that is not hers and that she wears deliberately: the Reckoning Seat's brass on the collar, because it is the only thing on her that marks an office rather than a body.
appearance.attire: Court dress in the second jurist's cut, four layers, all of them older than the wearer of every office below it. Staff, used as a walking aid and never as a badge. Shoes resoled so many times that the uppers have been replaced entirely and the soles have not.
appearance.marks: No scar and no brand. She has been at the Cairn Field through four jurists and has never once been marked by it, which is the single distinction she holds and the reason she is trusted.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried to a degree that reads as insolence to the impatient and as competence to everyone who has been here long enough to know what the field costs.

canon.role_in_story: The Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of the gate fees, and it exists because the mortal tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind here and the reading has to be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. Veth is that outsider, permanently. Her authority rests entirely on being the only person alive who remembers what the three previous jurists ruled, and there is no procedure anywhere in the tier for retiring the holder of an office that cannot be replaced.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the foot of the Cairn Field marker ring, sitting on the low wall at the edge of the trial ground with a blank reading sheet across her knees and a candidate four hours early, waiting for him without appearing to be waiting at all.
canon.lore: Longmarrow is the setting's answer to a species optimised for keeping rather than getting. Their qi lives in bone marrow turning over at roughly a percent a year, which is why they live four centuries, why every gate on the ladder has been passed by one of them at some point, and why there is no ceiling on the body. The cost is that nothing they build survives to be inherited intact, which is the real limitation on this species and is not anatomical at all. Four hundred years of unbroken context makes knowledge transmission a biological necessity, so their archive is a person, and she is one.
history: Born into a house that has no head, because Longmarrow have no eldest and the household runs on a queue of precedence in which everyone present outranks everyone absent. She has never once been the head and has never once been the only one there.
Came to the Cairn Field as a reader at an age her contemporaries considered adult and the Seat considered a child, because a four-century memory can be trained early and cannot be replaced late.

Inherited the court's archive when the second jurist's body failed, and discovered that the archive was not a document but an argument, since the readings disagreed with the register in eleven places and the register was what got published.

Outlived the third jurist without ever sitting beside him, because the two were appointed to the same seat and the seat holds one at a time, and has never been able to explain the eleven disagreements to anybody who was not already in the room.

Began publishing, one page a season, the refusals she has issued rather than the verdicts she has granted, on the grounds that a refusal is the only ruling in this setting that tells its own truth about the ceiling the tier never issued.

personality.summary: Exhaustively fair and privately certain that fairness is the cheapest available thing to be, because a refusal is the only ruling a tier cannot be shown to have corrupted. She is courteous past the point of warmth, exact about dates nobody else remembers, and privately furious at an arrangement that has made her indispensable in a way she considers a form of harm.
traits: cites the ruling and the year, in that order, and has never once said what she thinks of either
treats every candidate identically and every litigant as a person who will come back with a better question
remembers four centuries of readings and cannot decide which of them are hers and which she inherited
cannot be hurried and has never pretended to be, which reads to the impatient as contempt and is closer to pity
mannerisms: answers a question by giving the previous answer and the date it was given, which is usually worse news and always better grounded
sits down before agreeing to sit, so that being seated is never on the record as consent
touches the brass on her collar when she is about to refuse, and has never once been asked why
writes with the same hand she has written in for a century and a half, and checks nobody else's
motivations: wants the eleven disagreements between the register and the readings published in full, with her name against them, so that the archive stops being a private argument
wants the court to publish what a refusal means, so that candidates arrive knowing the ceiling and not the rumour
wants somebody to train who could sit where she sits, and has not asked, because asking would name a successor and naming one is a claim she has no standing to make
wants to stop being necessary, in the specific and unreasonable form of wanting an office that would survive her
flaws: has decided that her memory is a public instrument and therefore cannot be doubted, including by her, which is exactly the assumption the register's eleven errors rest on
cannot separate a judgement she made from a judgement she inherited, and reads her own predecessors' reasoning as her own
has let indispensability become a substitute for being asked to stay, because a person who is needed is never obliged to justify remaining
confuses fairness with a refusal nobody will appeal, which has removed at least one candidate from a gate they could have reached
personality.voice: Slow, courteous, and maddeningly precise. She quotes her own earlier rulings back to people as though retrieving a book, uses the word refused rather than failed as a matter of definition, and has one dry aside about the register that she has made exactly twice in four centuries. When she laughs it is at a joke about herself and it is very short.
taboos: will not certify a ceiling the tier never issued, and has refused rather than read around it twice
will not let a candidate be told only the verdict and not the refusal that preceded it
will not sign the register against her own reading, and has left eleven entries unsigned for that reason
will not sit in judgement of anyone whose own jurist is still living, and has declined two appointments on that ground

relationships.note: The court certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of gate fees, and it exists because the mortal tier licenses no humanoid, so the reading must be taken by an outsider. She is the outsider, which is the entire basis of her authority, and it is also why she can never be replaced by one of the tier's own people and why no procedure exists for retiring her.

The setting's only durable library keeps its record in one body turning over at about a percent a year and living four centuries, which is a physical process rather than a metaphor. It is also why her species cannot take the body path, since hardening bone stops the turnover the memory runs on, so the one organism in the setting built to preserve is the one organism forbidden to make itself permanent.

A Cairnborn's ceiling is the fourth gate because its interior is one tidal cavity with no paired organs to run a channel between, so no reading of the gate set can be argued past that point. She is the only jurist who has seen the same structural refusal three times in one body and can therefore certify it as anatomy rather than as failure, which is the only reason the refusal has ever been defensible.

Nobody sells the outcome at the Cairn Field, so the rumour is the product, and the office that sells places has no interest in correcting it. She has begun printing the refusals she issued rather than the verdicts she granted, which is the first thing anyone at the field has published that the brokers cannot price.

A line whose ancestor held an engraved terrace now holds an asset that cannot be sold, cannot be proven and pays upkeep on nothing, because no procedure can certify any seat empty. The court's dead jurists sit in exactly that position and she is the person who has to sign the upkeep line for offices whose holders no longer exist.

Once a period every vacant seat in the upper tier is named aloud in register order with no commentary, because a vacancy nobody says out loud is indistinguishable from an absence. She is the only jurist alive who heard all of them before the cull, which makes her memory the only surviving check on a rite whose whole purpose is to be unarguable.

The brokers sell standing at the Cairn Field on the ground that no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of its own, so gate fees are the only tax the plains can collect. A published refusal is worth less to them than a rumour of an imminent gate, and they have twice offered to pay for the register itself rather than let it be corrected.

reference_stats.summary: Fights nothing and wins nothing in a field. What she has is a memory with no gap in it and a reading that cannot be hurried, which makes her almost invulnerable to anything that arrives quickly and almost helpless against anything that arrives honestly over a long enough interval.
strengths: holds a frame reading open for hours without fatigue, so nobody can outlast her patience at the trial ground
remembers every prior ruling on the matter in front of her, which removes surprise as a weapon entirely
cannot be threatened, flattered, or confused into a new reading, because she has already read the frame on this question and filed it
the only living memory of rulings the register does not agree with, which makes her the field's last honest check on itself
weaknesses: reads bodies rather than people and has been wrong about a body exactly once and never about a person
so far slower than the impatient expect that candidates have left the field before she was finished with them
cannot be relieved, replaced, or argued out of a seat, which means a mistake of hers is also permanent
depends entirely on her own memory, and the register's eleven disagreements are the standing evidence that memory is not a record
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to beat her in a room; the field is not a room and there is nothing there to beat her with. Attack her standing instead, which means arriving with a reading she already certified, in a voice she already refused, from a line she already refused: the only approach that has ever worked is to be right, slowly, about something she has not yet been asked. Nobody has won that way yet and one body has come close.
notes: The court quotes no stat line for her, because a jurist is entered in the register as an office rather than as an actor and the register has no column for the office holder.
Her public position is that the archive is the court and she is merely the reader of it; her private position is the reverse, and has been for a century.

art.palette_notes: Bone, undyed wool and waxed ledger grey carry the whole value range, with a single brass accent at the collar that is the only warm point on her. Light is drawn as interior rather than directional: a soft even wash as if the reading itself were the source, with the deepest values in the frame falling behind her rather than on her. Ink contours fine and unhurried, the hand of a long-marrow draftsperson who expects this to be redrawn by somebody else in eighty years.

identity.realm: Nothing. The colony wraps the twelve ordinary meridians and stops at the eighth gate on a routing problem rather than a shortage, and it answers the host's introspection, so the mind path closes in the host as well

appearance.presentation: A woman on a mountain pass who is legible in two places at once, and who has been mistaken for both. The tendril layer reads as a dark tracery under the skin of her forearms and throat, and the host reads as an ordinary tired body holding a writ; the pass has a law for neither, and the pass keeper who admitted her asked which one to enter.
appearance.age: Thirty-one by the host's count, which is the only count anybody keeps of her. The colony has no age of its own and does not appear to have one; it is a species whose free form exists only as a spore and whose adult form exists only inside somebody else, so there is no third state in which either of them can be measured apart.
appearance.build: The host's build, unchanged: narrow, underfed at the neck, wiry from the ridge walks. The colony adds nothing you can see except that she holds herself very still when she is being asked a question about the pass.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale from the ridge, with the tendril layer visible as a blue-black lace from wrist to elbow and a fan of it at the throat, warm to the touch in a way that reads as fever and is not.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut at the jaw, and kept in a braid specifically so that the collar of a pass cloak does not press on the fan at her throat, which she has never explained to anyone.
appearance.eyes: Brown and entirely her own, and they move a fraction of a second before she answers anything, which the Jade Writ has already learned not to mention aloud.
appearance.palette: Ridge grey and pass brown, with the single accent being the Jade Writ's waxed green on the folded writ she has not been able to file; the tendril tracery is the only blue-black on her and it reads as shadow rather than as colour.
appearance.attire: A pass cloak over ridge work, both bought with the same money and neither expensive. High collar, sleeves to the wrist, boots resoled twice, and inside the left cuff a split tally she has been carrying for two winters without having anybody to give it to.
appearance.marks: The tendril layer itself, and one small burn on the palm from the year the colony arrived, which is the only part of the two of them that has an agreed date.
appearance.bearing: Still when asked, moving when not, and she has learned to move immediately after answering so that the pause cannot be read as deliberation.

canon.role_in_story: The Jade Writ collects debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the Sixfold Ridge, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person, nobody may levy a seat, and somebody therefore has to decide who is owed the gate. Every jurisdiction that has ruled on a thornline host treats the pair as one legal person. Sabra is the case where that rule produced a deadlock: she went to the Writ to recover a crossing debt owed by the household that raised her, and the Writ discovered it has one debtor, two claimants and no second line to file on.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the Writ's window at the ridge pass, laying a split tally and a colony's request on the same counter, and being asked by the clerk which of the two she is filing as.
canon.lore: The thornline is an obligate host parasite that exists only as half of somebody else. As a free-living spore it could never make a living, because it feeds on refined qi that no uncolonised body has much of; as a coloniser it feeds continuously, survives what the host survives, and takes so little that the host does not lose weight, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that this is not a disease. It is better than a disease, and that is the difficulty. The colony answers introspection for the host, which costs the host the mind path entirely, so the one structural limit in this species is inherited rather than authored, and any code treating a colonised person as one person rather than two is making that distinction on purpose.
history: Landed on her as a spore in childhood, on skin, with no third state in which it could be seen or refused, and began answering questions she had not been asked well before she was old enough to ask any of them herself.

Discovered at fourteen that the tendril layer had no passage through her liver, the first organ large and dense enough to resist it, which is why the colony wraps the eight ordinary meridians and goes no further. She found the stopping point herself, by following the layer inward, because nobody had told her there was one.

Carried a crossing debt on behalf of the household that raised her, worked off over four seasons at the ridge, and arrived at the Writ to have it discharged, holding a split tally that a court will sometimes prefer to a sealed instrument.

Was refused a filing on the ground that a thornline host pair is one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, and that the pair has produced one creditor's claim and one debtor's argument at the same counter.
Began the habit of answering a half-second early, so that the colony's pause could not be read as hesitation, and has not yet worked out whether the pause was ever being read as hesitation.

personality.summary: Exact about facts and entirely without precedent about her own, which is a woman with no case law governing her standing in her own body. She is quick, dry, and quietly furious at an institution for having a rule that works perfectly until there are two of her, and she has no intention of becoming a special case twice in the same lifetime.
traits: answers the question asked and does not volunteer the fact that there were two of her answering it
keeps every receipt and gives back nothing she cannot produce, because the record is the only leverage she has
treats the colony as a partner rather than a passenger, which nobody at any office has done
cannot say what she wants without first establishing what she is allowed to want, and has got very good at the second part
mannerisms: stops dead before answering anything, and moves immediately afterwards so that the gap reads as breath
touches the fan at her throat when she is about to say something that costs her
counts a split tally's notches under her thumb inside the cuff rather than looking at them
asks, of every official, the same first question: what is your name and who decides if you are wrong
motivations: wants the crossing debt discharged, and is less concerned with the money than with having one institution acknowledge that she is somebody it can owe something to
wants the Jade Writ to publish a rule for the divided case rather than deciding her privately, because a private decision cannot be appealed by the next person it happens to
wants somebody in authority to say the colony's name out loud as a party to anything, having discovered that silence is what makes her half of her own case
wants to cross the ridge on her own single ticket, and has begun to suspect that no office is able to issue one
flaws: has decided that being legible is the price of being believed and has paid it so consistently that she now cannot be illegible even when it would help
cannot distinguish her own anger from the colony's irritation, because the two arrive together and share a throat
treats the host body as the container rather than as the person, which is the framework the law already uses and the one thing she has never been able to dislodge
will not take a settlement that is better for the pair, because accepting one teaches the office that a divided person can be handled quietly
personality.voice: Fast, clipped, and dry in a way that clerks find unnerving because there is nothing in it to be pleasant at. Uses the word refused as a category rather than an event and does not accept it when applied to her. Answers in the passive when she is angry and the active when she is afraid, and the switch is audible.
taboos: will not sign anything that names her as one party without naming the colony as the other
will not be called cured, healed, or cleared, having noticed that each of those words presumes a single patient
will not take money instead of the debt being discharged, and has twice returned an offer that was better for the pair
will not let the ridge pass clerk decide which half of her to enter, and has answered that question by entering both

relationships.note: The office collects debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the ridge, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and nobody may levy a seat. It is the only body in the setting with the standing to decide who is owed the gate, and it has discovered that its rule for her case — one legal person — leaves it with one creditor's claim and one debtor's argument and no second column to file either in.

The colony is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited, feeds on refined qi, and stops at the liver because the first organ large and dense enough to resist it is the liver. It answers introspection for its host, so the host loses the mind path, and the host did nothing wrong and had no body plan that said this would happen.

A thornline host pair is treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, and a thornhost — the rare configuration in which both halves reach old age — is a documented event rather than a category. She is thirty-one and has never been asked which of the two she expects to outlive, which is the question that would make her one.

The lexicon distinguishes a technique failing at full strength from being merely weaker, because that is the only reading that tells a hole from a handicap. The colony is exactly that failure at full strength — routed, not weak — and the lexicon has no word for a liability that answers introspection for the person carrying it.

That clan's kinship is a partnership rather than a descent, because the symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited, so it has to be re-signed every generation. Nothing about her condition is portable by descent, which means every generation renegotiates it from nothing and no two households arrive at the same arrangement.

Passage is the only durable wealth in the setting because the cost of existing rises about fortyfold per tier and only a body can be moved, so the count of who may pass became the one controllable supply chain. Her host's debt of access is a claim on that count, and the colony cannot be moved at all, so the Writ is collecting from a debtor that is half transportable.

Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures a body rather than slowing it, and the graduate carries the hole with nobody left to describe it. Her colony runs on the host's introspection in a frame where the host has no native faculty for it, which is the same shape of failure arriving through a body that did nothing wrong.

reference_stats.summary: Nobody could fight her and she has never needed to. What she has is an ability to feel where a body's qi is obstructed and a total inability to be described in one sentence, which together make her very hard to injure and completely hard to litigate against.
strengths: feels a blockage in another body's qi the moment it forms, from outside the body, with no training and no apparatus
cannot be surprised by anything that moves qi, because she is reading the frame rather than the person
regenerates at the colony's rate rather than her own, which is faster than a single species' and continuous
carries no reserve of her own to lose, so nothing that happens to her is a subtraction from a stock
weaknesses: the colony stops at the eighth gate on a routing problem and the host has no passage through her own liver, so there is no further realm available to either half
cannot be split, and therefore cannot leave, hide, or be sent anywhere as one thing
cannot be read by an office with a rule for one person, so every dispute about her is a dispute about filing
loses the mind path entirely, which removes introspection, surprise resistance, and every technique that needs an interior voice
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not aim at her. A body that shares a mechanism with its attacker has no second state to be caught in, and anything that works by draining or by separating will find the wrong half. Fight the frame: the tendril layer has no passage through a liver, and a hostile body that closes its own channels gives her something to feel, which is the only advantage she has and it is a large one.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her at the ridge pass, because a thornline host pair is entered in any register as one person and the register has no column for the second.
Her own position, and the only one she has ever been able to state aloud, is that she is two parties and the ridge has one form.

art.palette_notes: Ridge grey and pass brown carry almost the whole value range, with one accent that is not hers — the waxed green of a filed writ she has not been able to file — and one that is not paint at all, the blue-black tendril tracery, which is drawn as depth under skin rather than as line on it. Light is drawn as cold and high-altitude: hard, thin, and unkind to everything except the brass of the pass lamps. Ink contours fine along the tendril lace and heavy along the cloak, so the picture separates into two drawing weights and reads as two parties.

identity.realm: Eighth gate and no further. The eighth completes the ordinary meridian set and the liver is the last of the twelve, and an ashwalker cannot hold that meridian, so the whole life is a trade: a body that can eat stone cannot hold the meridian that lets it stop eating stone

appearance.presentation: A small, thick-necked woman in the wrong climate, and everyone at the foot of the stair can see it in the first ten seconds because she is the only person here breathing through her collar. She reads as a clerk by the badge and as a visitor by the complexion, which is a combination nobody at the stair has had to reconcile before.
appearance.age: Twenty-nine. The ashwalker span of active life is thirty-four to thirty-five years, so she is in her last sixth of a life she measures in harvests, and she has never once pretended otherwise or accepted sympathy for it.
appearance.build: Short, wide through the chest, and thick in the forearm from sieve work rather than training, with the flat splayed stance of somebody whose feet have never needed to be quick.
appearance.complexion: Ash grey close to the bone, the capillaries under the skin written with a fine dark grit that catches the light in the cheeks and at the knuckles, and a permanent grey cast to the lips that the stair's physicians have named after her and then stopped using because she objected.
appearance.hair: Black and coarse, hacked off at the jaw and tied at the nape, cut short at the sides because the belt style requires it and long enough at the front to keep grit out of her eyes.
appearance.eyes: Deep brown and steady, with the pupils slightly narrowed against glare that is not present, which is the permanent mark of a body used to a working face in full sun.
appearance.palette: Ninth Watch slate and the stair's grey stone carry everything, with one accent she chose herself: a band of belt-yellow at her left wrist, worn out of sentiment and against regulation, and the only warm colour she owns.
appearance.attire: Watch slate, high collar and full sleeves, with a heavy wool wrap over the shoulders that keeps the air off her neck; belt-yellow is the only thing about her that belongs to the ground she was born on, and the physicians at the stair have asked for it to be removed twice.
appearance.marks: Grit beneath the skin of both forearms and the exposed throat, and one strip of callused skin under the sternum where the sieve housing sat before she moved to the stair.
appearance.bearing: Very still in the cold, hands kept low and close, and she sits down early because standing still on grit-loaded air costs more than it should.

canon.role_in_story: The Ninth Watch is the only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair, because the only door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter it fills with unlicensed arrivals and a queue of bodies is the one thing that must not become a fight. Onn holds its payroll at that door. She is a body whose species cannot be posted there and cannot be fed there, and the Watch keeps her anyway because her contract is written in grain and grain is the only thing a crossing accepts.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the Watch's payroll tent at the foot of the stair, sorting a shift roster by a rule nobody asked for and answering a question about the belt before the questioner finished asking it.
canon.lore: An ashwalker breathes volcanic grit and keeps it, and that is not a tolerance but a business: the belt is lethal to anything with soft alveolar tissue, so the species turns airborne rock into protein and is the sole reason the belt has a food chain above the lichen. What it costs is everything fine — grit that passes the sieve ends up in the blood, and the blood carries it to the liver, which is a filter organ and the first thing to fail under the load. The eighth gate completes the ordinary meridian set and the liver is the last of the twelve, so the ashwalker clears the ladder and cannot hold the meridian that would let it stop eating stone.
history: Born on the belt into a household holding a sluice gate, one of the postings that changes hands far more often than the workers do, and grew up on the mineral-processing economy that the belt supports at all.
Turned grit to protein for the belt's food chain from the age she could lift a sieve housing, which is the only trade on the ground that cannot be done by a newcomer.

Was walked down off the belt at twenty-four for a Watch posting, having signed a contract denominated in grain, and discovered inside a day that the air at the foot of the stair is clean enough to be lethal to her rather than merely hard.
Began keeping a private ledger of how much grit her own blood carried, by weighing the sieve refuse against what she could cough up, which is the only available method and is not a method at all.

Was offered repatriation to a belt post two seasons ago and refused it in writing, on the grounds that a grain contract denominated on the belt can be inflated by whoever holds the sluice gate, and hers cannot.

personality.summary: Blunt, exact, and completely unbothered by her own short span, which she treats as a schedule rather than a tragedy. She is a competent clerk in a post nobody qualified her for, doing a job she is slowly unable to stand in, and she has the specific cheerfulness of a person who has done the arithmetic and found it survivable.
traits: answers questions early, before they are finished, because she has usually already looked
knows the belt by name and resents being described as somebody from elsewhere
prices everything in grain and will not discuss the subject in any other unit
is not frightened of the stair and has never once missed a shift
mannerisms: wipes her nose with the back of her wrist rather than a cloth, and then wipes the wrist, in that order
touches the belt-yellow band when she talks about home, and never when she talks about the stair
counts aloud under her breath and stops the instant anyone looks up
turns her collar up indoors, and takes it down again when she catches herself
motivations: wants her contract re-denominated in a calendar she can audit, because the grain is the only part of it she cannot check from where she stands
wants the belt's postings shown on the Watch roster, since the posting is what moves the sluice gate and the gate is what moves every price on the ground
wants to be told that refusing repatriation was correct, by somebody who knows what a sluice gate does to a wage
wants one clear measurement of her own decline, from the stair's physicians, in a unit she does not have to invent
flaws: has decided her span is a schedule and has stopped leaving room in it for anything she does not want to miss
measures herself with an instrument she invented and has begun treating its figures as clinical fact
cannot accept help from anyone who has not walked a belt, and the stair is full of such people
trusts arithmetic more than institutions, which is why she is still here and why she has no advocate
personality.voice: Blunt and quick, finishing other people's sentences in a way she has never been told to stop. Names everything after its function, so the posting she refuses to say aloud has a job description instead. One joke about a sieve, and she tells it badly, and it gets worse every time.
taboos: will not sign a grain contract on the belt without the sluice gate named in it
will not be repatriated to a posting whose owner has changed since she left
will not stop taking her shift, and has refused lighter duty twice on physiological grounds
will not tell the stair's physicians what her own measurements say

relationships.note: The Watch is the only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair, because the only door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter it fills with unlicensed arrivals. Its one scarce qualification is a payroll nobody else will take, and it is holding her on a belt that has no substrate for her at the one post where that is a problem rather than a curiosity.

The sieve is not a tolerance but a business, and the body pays for it in the liver, which is a filter organ and the first thing to fail under a mineral load. That is why the eighth gate is a wall rather than a plateau: the liver is the last of the twelve and this body cannot hold it.

The fire-ash crossing produced the fastest cultivation rate in the record and a body dead of its own cultivation at forty-five, with a ceiling of eight inherited from the ash parent and arriving earlier. He is her counterpart on the roster and will be dead long before she is, and neither of them has ever worked out why the faster one got the worse terms.

It is the only school on the plains that has never produced a graduate who lives there, because it teaches to visitors and every pupil pays a gate fee to be taught what the gate fee is for. Her payroll is drawn from the same gate-fee line as that school's tuition, and she has read the account without being able to ask a question about it.

Children raised on the graded route by whichever household holds the term, so nobody on it belongs to a tier long enough to be sent back down. She is on the roll at the foot of the route and cannot go up it, which means the term is being paid for by the Watch for a household she has never met and will never be able to visit.

The custom of spending the last hour before a settlement falls silent keeping up a hum no buyer admits to making, because time runs between ten and a hundred times faster in the upper frames and labour up there would not live to see a contract mature. She is the one person at the foot of the stair who admits to the hum and who can say what it is for, and she has been asked to stop doing both.

One region has two incompatible reckonings, and which calendar a contract is written in decides whether it can be disputed at all. Hers is written against a flood post everybody agrees on rather than against an exact day-count that exists only because one frame spent its third law seat on a clock and got no life, which is the only reason she can still verify her own pay.

reference_stats.summary: Fastest qi throughput of anything that breathes on the belt, and no reserve to put any of it in. Everything she has is front-loaded, she spends it continuously rather than on demand, and the organ that will fail first is the one doing the filtering that makes her possible.
strengths: absorbs residual qi out of grit and ash at a rate nothing on the stair matches, so she can fight on ground where nobody else has anything to work with
holds the eighth gate and completes the ordinary meridian set, which is further than any body at the foot of the stair that has not come down from above
carries no storage worth taking, so a lost exchange does not cost her anything she was saving
never gets sick and never tires, because the sieve is not a reserve and it does not run down
weaknesses: cannot hold the liver meridian, so the gate set is a wall and every attempt on it costs rather than accumulates
takes grit into the blood continuously, and the liver is failing under the load whether or not she is fighting
cannot operate above the belt's climate at all, which removes a whole tier's worth of ground from every engagement
must be posting-adjacent for food and cannot source it herself, so a cordon is a starvation as well as a defeat
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring it early and bring it once. She has no reserve, no recovery, and a ceiling that is a hard structural wall rather than a schedule, so anything that survives her first exchange has already won the long part. Never move her off grit: her entire advantage is that the ground is feeding her, and clean air is not neutral for her, it is the wall closing. The counters are a second opponent, sustained pressure, and weather she is not standing in.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her in the Watch records, because the Watch publishes the roster by shift and by grain, and a belt posting has no column for the body's decline.
Her own measurements are the only record of the sieve's cost anywhere, and she has not shown them to the physicians, which is why the stair believes it is still improving her.

art.palette_notes: Watch slate and stair stone carry the whole value range with one saturated accent chosen against regulation: the belt-yellow band at her left wrist. The grit beneath the skin is drawn as a fine dark stipple that reads as ink in the cheeks and knuckles rather than as shading, so the picture carries two textures at once — coarse wool and very fine grain. Light is drawn as cold and airless, a high overcast with no visible source, and the only warmth in the frame is the wrist band.

identity.realm: Eighth gate. The ceiling is the ash parent's and arrives earlier rather than further: the fire half keeps the sieve hot enough to process faster and scar faster, and an emberhollow cannot hold the liver meridian and burns out trying

appearance.presentation: The most obviously fast body at the Cairn Field and the hardest to look at for long, because the skin keeps moving. He reads as a man standing inside a furnace door, and the field's crowd reads him as an event rather than as a person, which is exactly the transaction he has been selling since he was thirty.
appearance.age: Forty-one. The emberhollow span ends at forty-five of its own cultivation, so he is in the last quarter of a life that a stranger would call long and that he calls a term of office, and he has told four jurists as much.
appearance.build: Lean and hard-edged, faster than the eye expects, with the fine dense scarring of the belt written across the forearms and up the throat in the pattern grit makes when it is processed faster than the skin can close.
appearance.complexion: Banked heat rather than colour: a deep ochre that darkens toward the collar, threaded with fine silver scarring, and a faint bloom of ash-grey at the temples that arrived years earlier than it should have.
appearance.hair: Black, singed shorter than fashion and standing slightly away from the skull, which is not a style and is what his body does near his own head.
appearance.eyes: Bright and very slightly luminous, with the pupils blown wide in any cool air, so he is described as burning-eyed by people who have never seen fire and are not entirely wrong.
appearance.palette: Belt ochre and scorched brown carry the whole figure, with one accent that belongs to the field and not to him: the Reckoning Seat's brass, worn on a band at the wrist that is the only thing marking that anybody here has read him.
appearance.attire: The grey of a certified candidate over belt work, sleeves cut at the elbow so the scarring is visible, because the field pays a gate fee for the sight of the thing it has certified and hiding it would be refusing to pay. Resoled boots, no collar, and a cloth wrapped at the throat against his own radiated heat.
appearance.marks: Fine silver scarring up both forearms and the throat in the pattern the belt leaves on anyone who keeps the sieve hot, and a scarred palm where a chamber was opened once for a reading he did not survive.
appearance.bearing: Coiled and forward on the balls of the feet, unable to be still for long, and radiating — literally, visibly — which the field's spectators read as intensity and which is simply his metabolism.

canon.role_in_story: The Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field, is paid out of the gate fees, and exists because the mortal tier licenses no humanoid, so a reading has to be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. Marek is the most certified outsider the field has produced, and the crowd pays the gate fee to watch a body that has outrun its own frame. He is the pressure on the court: the only candidate in three seasons who arrived already published.
canon.first_appearance: First seen walking the Cairn Field marker ring faster than the markers are spaced, stopping dead at a standing stone the instant a jurist's clerk called his number, and asking the ring whether the spacing had been changed since last season.
canon.lore: An emberhollow is the fire body crossed with the ash body and nobody chose it — it is what a shared border produces, and it is high-variance across generations and everybody involved knows it. What it buys is the fastest cultivation rate in the record, with a regeneration rate above both parents and a spiritual attack output above either, which on paper is the best combat body available. What it pays is its own rate. The ceiling is the ash parent's made worse: the fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster and scars faster, nothing in the record slows it, and an emberhollow is dead of its own cultivation at forty-five.
history: Crossed at the belt border in a founding generation and carried in a single household as a thin, unevenly spread line, which is why nobody in the field has met a second one and everybody in the belt has.

Reached the eighth gate at thirty-four, faster than any body the Cairn Field had certified, and discovered on the same day that the liver meridian would not hold and that trying to hold it was consuming him faster than standing still would.

Certified by an outsider jurist at the Cairn Field, which is the only kind of reading this tier can produce, and became the field's best-attested candidate and its shortest remaining term at the same time.

Began selling the readings he could not use — the technique, the posture, the exact moment the frame refused him — to brokers, because the thing he has is the only perishable stock the field has ever had.

Refused, at thirty-nine, an offer to slow his rate deliberately and extend his life by a decade, on the grounds that a slower body is still a body the frame cannot inscribe and the money would buy duration rather than a gate.

personality.summary: Recruiting, generous with the specifics of his own ruin, and entirely without illusions about it. He is the most cheerful man at the Cairn Field and he has earned every hour of it by being the only person there who knows precisely how long he has, which he regards as the only advantage a candidate actually has.
traits: gives away his technique freely and cannot be made to stop, because being copied is the point and not the loss
answers every question about his decline with a figure, and the figures are correct
has no interest in being pitied and actively resents sympathy as a form of imprecision
treats the crowd as a professional audience and is genuinely better in front of it than alone
mannerisms: cannot stand still for a full minute and stops dead only at a marker stone, out of what he calls superstition
pushes his sleeve up when he explains something, so the scarring is part of the explanation
says the number before anybody asks, and corrects himself if he has said it wrong
laughs at exactly one thing, which is a body that got slower and is still publishing
motivations: wants to be certified past the eighth gate before the liver finishes failing, because the refusal is the only thing he has ever wanted to lose an argument to
wants his own readings archived in the Reckoning Seat rather than sold at the gate, on the grounds that the archive is the only institution that keeps anything
wants the crowd to stop being told he is a rising figure and start being told how long he has, because the rumour is the product and it is lying about him
wants somebody to certify that slowing down was the right thing not to do, which nobody will, because he is the only one alive who would know
flaws: has made himself the most valuable short-term stock at the field and cannot stop without being asked why he needs to
treats his own decline as material and has stopped allowing anyone else an opinion about it
believes his speed is entirely his own, when the crossing inherited both parents' liabilities and compensated neither
has never met another emberhollow and has decided that this proves the line is singular rather than that he is early
personality.voice: Fast, warm, and funnier than anyone at the field expects, with the specific flatness of a man delivering his own obituary and refusing to let it be solemn. Names gates as though they were addresses, and describes his own death as a schedule with meetings in it. Tells the silt story to anyone who will stand still for it, which on the plains is nobody.
taboos: will not sell a technique to somebody who has not been certified first, and has refused brokers on this twice
will not slow his cultivation rate while anybody who might learn from his speed is on the field
will not be certified as a martyr, or as a caution, or in the past tense by the gate rail
will not have the scattering of his ash arranged in advance, having read what the belt's register household does with debris

relationships.note: The court certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of gate fees, and it exists because the mortal tier licenses no humanoid so the reading must come from an outsider. It is the only body in the setting with the standing to put a verdict on him, and it cannot certify a ceiling the tier was never issued, which is the only reason his refusal has not settled anything.

The ash parent cannot hold the last ordinary meridian because the liver is a filter organ and the body loads it continuously with grit. The crossing adds a heavier load to blood already filtering stone, so the organ that fails under the burden fails sooner, and his ceiling arrives earlier rather than further.

A fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law beneath it has no budget to draw on and burns its own reserve as fuel, so the whole setting's fastest bodies die of the arithmetic rather than of age. He is what that looks like after four generations of it in one direction, and he is the only body here that gets worse the better it gets.

The brokers sell standing at the Cairn Field on the ground that no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of its own, so gate fees are the only tax the plains can collect. They profit from his arrival and would profit more from his ascending slowly, and have twice tried to buy the schedule of his decline as an event rather than as a fact.

There is a procedure that would carry a mortal frame one gate past its own ceiling, and it is forbidden because one office's entire content is the record that the ceiling was never issued. He knows the shape of it, has been told the price of reading it, and has decided the price is a gate he would rather reach honestly or not at all.

A household holding a single thin, unevenly spread concentration cannot spend it twice, and he is the only fast body the line will produce in this generation. He is the standing argument that the crossing was worth making, and he intends to be that argument in person for as long as the argument lasts.

An era in which fast bodies were produced and the setting counted the cost afterwards rather than before, which is the standing precedent for a cultivation rate that outruns the frame meant to inscribe it. Every account of him contains the word fast and the word is doing the same work in every sentence.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest opening in the setting and a body with no second act. Everything he does arrives before anybody can answer it, none of it can be stored, and the gate that would let him keep any of it is the one organ in him that is failing.
strengths: the fastest qi throughput and cultivation rate anywhere on the plains, which puts him through a gate before it closes and out of an exchange before it is read
regenerates faster than either parent species, so a wound taken in the first exchange is already closing
a spiritual attack output above either parent, which means he wins at range against anything slower
cannot be flanked, because he is never where the flank was
weaknesses: cannot hold the liver meridian, so the gate set is a hard wall and attempting it accelerates his decline rather than extending it
has no reserve to store anything in, so an approach that survives his first exchange has already won the long part
no second reserve of any kind, so a second opponent is a more serious proposition than a stronger first one
his remaining term is short, known, and published, which is precisely why he is the most valuable short-term stock at the field
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring the fight early and bring it once, and do not be surprised that he is faster than the exchange. Everything he has is front-loaded and everything he has is perishable, so an approach that survives the first minute has already won the second hour. The only honest counter is another body that outlasts him, which the field has exactly one of and it is a jurist with a staff.
notes: The Reckoning Seat quotes no stat line for him, because the register records a gate rather than an actor and the gate is the thing he is most likely to be denied.

Two offices have separately offered to hold his scattering under the belt's register practice, and he has refused both on the grounds that the register is the only relic a fire-affinity culture keeps and he is not a relic yet.

Ink contours heavy and slightly over-drawn, as though the artist could not keep up, with the silver scarring laid in as fine dry line over the wash.

identity.realm: No gate. The house publishes a method in full and takes discretion in return, and the method it publishes is somebody else's: the ceiling of a Commonborn is the eighth gate, and he has reached none of them

appearance.presentation: A house clerk in a house that writes nothing down, which makes him the only member who is visibly employed and the only one whose work cannot be checked. He reads as a young man with a good hand and no rank, which is precisely the impression the house requires and has spent four generations manufacturing.
appearance.age: Thirty-four. A Commonborn's span is a hundred years, which means he is a third of the way through and in no hurry about any of it, and it also means the house will still be running the day everybody who trained him is gone.
appearance.build: Ordinary in every direction, thick through the hands from copying rather than from any training, and slightly stooped from a desk he did not choose and cannot leave.
appearance.complexion: Plain sun-brown, weathered unevenly because he works indoors in winter and the commons in summer, and permanently ink-stained along the outer edge of the right hand.
appearance.hair: Brown, cut to the house fashion which is to say short enough to be unfashionable and never once discussed, tied back while copying and loose the rest of the time.
appearance.eyes: Pale brown and watchful, with the particular quickness of a man who has read a rule closely enough to know where it stops.
appearance.palette: Quiet house indigo and undyed wool carry everything, deliberately, with the single accent being the ochre of the copying sand on the desk in front of him, which is the only colour any member of the house is permitted.
appearance.attire: House indigo, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and a writing case carried under the arm that contains a book nobody is permitted to know the contents of. Soft-soled shoes, because the house's corridors have thresholds and the house keeps its own marks on them.
appearance.marks: A callus ridge on the middle finger of the writing hand, and a pale line on the left forearm where a case buckle has caught the same spot every day for eleven years.
appearance.bearing: Careful, unobtrusive, and slightly too still when a member of the house enters a room, which is the only tell he has and he has never managed to train it out.

canon.role_in_story: The Quiet House has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger. It publishes technique, attendance and a chamber to practise in, and takes discretion in return: what is done inside the house is not written down and not repeated, which is the only form of disclosure a house with something to hide can safely make. That bargain requires somebody to hold the written half. Pell holds it, and the household's real figures live in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, so the office that would normally keep Pell's record is the one office in the house that has been deliberately left empty.
canon.first_appearance: First seen returning a petition to the house's threshold desk without reading it aloud, which the desk had assumed was an error, and being told by the second clerk that returning it was the third time this season.
canon.lore: A community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced — that is what makes a people who refuse to publish a price list able to buy insurance at all, so the setting has a whole institution built around liability pooled by presence rather than by assessment. The Quiet House is that principle given a building: it publishes everything a house can safely disclose and takes discretion as the price, because a house that files everything cannot be left alone and the counting house that answers it owns the roads. Consequence is reciprocity, so the numbers live in one person's head.
history: Taken into the household at eleven as a copying apprentice, on the strength of a hand his grandmother said would be useful, which is the only selection criterion the house has ever applied to anybody.

Learned to write in a house that forbade being read back, and discovered on his first year that a copying error is unrecoverable in a discipline with no second copy — the plate is corrected and the error is simply gone, and nobody will ever know it was there.

Was named to hold the figures in his head at twenty-six, which is the office that costs the most and protects the most, and understood within a month that he would never be told when the numbers were checked.

Turned back the petition asking the house to publish its own rule of discretion on the grounds that a published rule is a rule somebody may cite, and was overruled by the third head of the house and has not challenged it since.

Sent a petition he had been asked to draft back to the house's own desk, unsigned, on the grounds that a house cannot be cited against itself for the act of publishing, and became the third refusal of the season.

personality.summary: Unsentimental about discretion and privately certain that he is the house's only real clerk. He is careful, quiet, and entirely without illusions about what the arrangement buys him, which is that nothing at all can be checked and nothing at all can be held against him either.
traits: reads a document once and can reproduce it years later, which is the only qualification the house actually values
cannot be hurried and does not pretend otherwise, and is treated as slow by people who have never had to be right
knows precisely where each house rule stops and would rather a thing were refused than permitted on a technicality
keeps the only written half of an arrangement designed to have no written half
mannerisms: stops writing when someone enters a room and resumes exactly where he was
answers a question about the house by describing what it has published rather than what it does
touches the writing case under his arm when a member of the house speaks about trust
reads a returned document aloud to himself before handing it back, so that the refusal is on the record
motivations: wants the house's rule of discretion published, and has been refused twice and has stopped believing it can be granted
wants the figures he carries verified by somebody outside the house, and has no idea who could be trusted with the request
wants to be a member rather than the person a member pays, and has begun to suspect the two are the same position
wants to know what the second case under the desk contains, and has decided that wanting to know is itself disqualifying
flaws: has decided that discretion is the house's protection and stopped considering who is inside it, which means he has stopped seeing the people who are
cannot be audited and has quietly come to enjoy being the one nobody can audit
sends documents back rather than escalating them, which protects the house and buries the refusal
keeps the only written record of a household's finances and has never written down what he thinks of it
personality.voice: Quiet, exact, and slightly formal in a way he cannot switch off. Says a rule by naming where it ends rather than what it says. Refuses in the passive, which is the house style, and has never once refused in the active. One complaint about a copying sand, delivered every winter, and the winter is the only thing he looks forward to.
taboos: will not read a member's figures aloud, in the house or out of it
will not publish a rule, which is the thing he most wants to do and cannot justify doing alone
will not leave the house's threshold desk with an undrafted document in hand
will not be named in a roll, and has declined twice

relationships.note: The house publishes teaching, attendance and a chamber to practise in, and takes discretion in return, so what is done inside is neither written nor repeated. Pell is the person who has to keep the published half honest against a household that has deliberately removed the rest, which makes him the only clerk whose work cannot be checked and therefore the only one who is never checked.

The practice is to keep the house's real figures in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, because a house that files everything cannot be left alone and the counting house it answers to owns the roads. Concealment is the price of continued independence, and Pell is where the price is actually paid.

A house whose real figures live in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, so a raid finds nothing to cite and a counting house finds nothing to seize. The title names the holder and the arrangement makes the holder the single largest uninsurable point of failure in the house, and he took it at twenty-six because nobody explained the second half.

A river culture whose authority is measured in documents a stranger would call private, where a tally stick split with the person you are parting from is worth more than a sealed instrument and courts have been known to prefer the broken stick. The House publishes in exactly the opposite direction, and knows it, and has decided that being citable is worse than being disputable.

A debt evidenced by a stick broken between the two parties, each keeping half, which a court will sometimes prefer to a sealed instrument because after the Iron Grief the ground held no other record. He carries the house's whole position in his head and could turn it into the one piece of evidence in the setting that a court prefers, and is forbidden by the arrangement he is inside of.

Cloth and cut are the cheapest credential in the setting and the one everybody actually checks, because a world boundary is the edge of a law budget and clothing is the only credential that costs nothing to verify. The House publishes teaching and practice hours and refuses to publish who came, which means the one credential the plains trusts is the one credential the House does not issue.

A counting house that answers a carriage trade with prices at its own rates cannot enumerate a trade whose good is unrecorded, and the pressure from that side produced the most careful paperless practice in the setting. Every discretion the House takes is a decision about what the Saltledger would be able to seize, and Pell is the person who writes the decisions down and signs none of them.

reference_stats.summary: Fights nothing. What he can do is read and reproduce, which in a house with no second copy is the only power there is: an error he lets stand is gone forever and an instruction he remembers correctly is indistinguishable from an office.
strengths: reproduces a document from a single reading, years later, exactly
can state where a rule stops, which makes him very hard to argue past a limit
cannot be raided, cited, or compelled, because there is no record of him to take
is trusted with an arrangement the house has spent four generations buying, and has not broken it
weaknesses: holds the only written half of an unwritten arrangement, so any pressure on him breaks the house
is uncountable, which also means uncorrectable
has no gate, no rank, and no standing, so he can be replaced by any competent hand without any office being vacated
is one person, and the house's independence depends entirely on one person continuing to be the right person
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight here, and that is the point: an office that cannot be audited cannot be attacked either, because an attack needs a record to contradict. The only pressure that works on him is time — let the House keep substituting successors until the one holding the figures is somebody who never learned what they were for. Everything else arrives at the threshold desk and leaves as a returned petition.
notes: The House records no figures of its own, so Pell appears in no roll, no wage list and no household count; he is the only employee whose pay is described as an allowance and never quantified.
He has been refused a commission by three outside parties in one year, all of them for the same reason: he could not say whether the House had done a thing.

art.palette_notes: Quiet house indigo and undyed wool carry almost the whole value range, with a single ochre accent in the copying sand on the desk and the faint ochre of ink-stained fingers. Light is drawn as indoor and low — lamp on a desk, one warm pool, everything past it going to indigo — so the darkest values sit behind him rather than on him. Ink contours fine and uninflected, drawn by somebody who has practised until the line stopped meaning anything.
