identity.realm: Ninth gate by inheritance and no further. The line's grant is a defensive burn that fires continuously, so the body holds longer than a common frame and stops there, which is exactly why the guild has never been able to train somebody through him

appearance.presentation: A man who reads as a wall that got up, and who has decided that this is more efficient than correcting people. He is the only body at the Hollow Measure with the density of the mineral line and the reflexes of the fire line, and the combination is legible in every line of him: heavy, quick, and about sixty years long.
appearance.age: Forty-one. A stonebound's span is sixty years against the fire parent's fifty and the mineral parent's three hundred and fifty, which makes it the most durable crossing anyone can build and two thirds short of the mineral one, and there is no configuration of this crossing that fixes it.
appearance.build: Very heavy and very fast, shoulders like a lintel with the forearms of someone who has trained, standing slightly forward so the weight is already loaded.
appearance.complexion: Grey-flecked stone-pale with the mineral's dry sheen, overlain by a heat flush across the collarbone that the mineral half has nowhere to put, so it sits on the surface.
appearance.hair: Iron black and coarse, kept cropped hard at the jaw because the density of his skull makes anything else impossible, singed at the left temple from the forge floor.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady, with the heat behind them visible in low light as a faint internal line that is not a reflection.
appearance.palette: Quarrywright indigo-black and ash grey carry the whole figure, with one accent that is the seam: the raw ochre of an unrefined assay chip worn at his belt, which is a working tool and not a badge.
appearance.attire: Quarry indigo over boiled leather, both cut close and both enormously heavy, with a full-body harness that takes a stranger's weight off the frame at the cost of the body's own speed. Resoled boots and a pit helmet he never wears and always carries.
appearance.marks: A mineral seam running the length of the left forearm where the frame did not fully harden, and a burn at the left temple that he has never bothered to have treated because the mineral half regenerates it overnight.
appearance.bearing: Immobile at rest and startlingly quick in motion, with the specific fidget of a body that is too dense for the space it is in and would rather be working.

canon.role_in_story: The Quarrywright works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, and it exists because ore is the one thing on the plains a core can be caged in and because the work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body it employs is a visitor. Drust holds the lease on a working face and stands on his own ground as a visitor, because a visitor's claim cannot be held long enough to become a right. He is the fourth holder of that lease in three years and the first who has signed it on behalf of the guild rather than the household.
canon.lore: A stonebound is the documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body. The crossing is not remarkable; what is remarkable is that the resulting line was kept and named, which is what a lineage does. Inheritance is asymmetric and always will be: the mineral parent donates the ceiling and the durability, the fire parent donates the throughput and nothing else. The yin-organ gate needs two distinct organs with a channel between them, the stone half has one cavity, and heat is not a second organ.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the face lip with the assay board already chalked, refusing a promotion on the grounds that the figure on the board would not have gone up before the sale closed, and being asked by the guild clerk which of the three previous reeves had taught him that.
history: Carried the Ember Cradle's single thin concentration at a founding generation and held a seat in the household without ever being its fastest member, which for a body with two parents' outputs is a permanent condition.
Inherited a working-face lease at twenty-nine, signed on the household's behalf and stood on ground the frame considers foreign with the understanding that no native body is licensed to work it.

Lost three previous reeves in eleven years of the lease to the same event: the face at a depth where the densest bodies stop one gate short of their own tier, and the ninth gate being the last one the line can reach.
Refused the guild's offer to train him past the ninth gate by substitution, on the grounds that a mineral frame's cavity is the reason the gate is shut and no technique opens a second organ.
Began signing the assay disclosure himself before every sale at the face, a practice the guild calls unusual and the assay floor calls the only reason it may continue.

personality.summary: Blunt, immovable in every sense he can act on, and quietly certain that a lease is a temporary thing that he is honouring in full. He reads as stubborn until he says the phrase that a claim must be able to expire, and after that he reads as the only person on the face thinking about next year.
traits: refuses a promotion that would cost the face its assay practice, and does not consider this remarkable
treats the lease as a loan rather than a title, and behaves exactly as though somebody will end it
is faster than every other body at the flats and spends it carrying rather than fighting
cannot be frightened and does not pretend to be
mannerisms: sets both feet before he answers a question about weight
checks the helmet he is carrying and not the one he is wearing
answers a question about his line with a figure about the lease, because he has found it ends the conversation
stands between a person and the face rather than in front of them
motivations: wants the lease to expire on its own terms rather than be revoked, and is one year from being able to say it is working
wants the assay disclosure printed before every sale and kept unedited, and has defeated one attempt to stop it
wants a body that can hold a lease for the length of a working life, and knows his own sixty is not one
wants to be told that signing on the guild's behalf rather than the household's was correct
flaws: has decided that being heavy is a kind of honesty and uses it to end arguments, which works more often than it should
cannot distinguish between his own preference and the guild's interest, and they have agreed for so long that he no longer checks
treats the previous three reeves as a cost of doing business rather than as three people
is two thirds short of the lifespan of the mineral line he carries and has never once said so aloud
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and given to answering a question with a weight rather than a sentence. Uses the word visitor about himself without irony and without emphasis, which is the most unsettling thing about him. One joke, about the lease, and he tells it the same way every time.
taboos: will not sign a lease that cannot be ended
will not let a sale close before the assay figure is on the board
will not take a ninth gate from a substitute body and call it his own
will not tell a visitor they are at home

relationships.note: The guild works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, and the work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body it employs is a visitor and every visitor's claim has to expire. He is the fourth holder of one face lease in eleven years, and he is the only reeve who signed it for the guild rather than the household that had held it before him.

The densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of their own tier, and every holder of a working face profits from that hole staying a hole. He stops two gates lower and for the same family of reason, which means the face he works is inside the explanation and the office he holds is a consequence of it.

The measured quantity of stone left per unit of ground worked is published before any sale and never after, and it has been falling for three generations. Publishing the figure is what keeps both the disclosure and the reason unavailable, and he has made signing it part of the act of selling rather than a courtesy attached to it.

A Cairnborn's interior is one tidal cavity with no paired organs, so the yin-organ gate is shut for want of two structures rather than for want of strength. He carries that same shut gate in a body that is otherwise the most capable on the flats, which is the whole content of the crossing and the reason heat does not count as a second organ.

A fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law beneath it eats its own reserve as fuel and dies in decades, while a mineral line lives for centuries and cannot make itself permanent. He is both of those liabilities in one frame, and the crossing compensated neither, so the most durable body anyone can build dies at sixty.

That clan holds the lease on a working face and stands on its own ground as a visitor, because nothing native to the mortal tier is licensed to work a seam, so the lease has to expire every season. A claim that could not be revoked would become a right, and a right on ground the frame calls foreign is the one thing the tier cannot have.

A debt carried on a stick broken between the two parties is the only evidence a community here can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe, and after the Iron Grief the ground held no other record. His lease is held on guild paper at a face three reeves deep, and he has offered to break the stick with the next holder and been refused by the guild.

reference_stats.summary: The densest body at the flats with the reflexes of the fire line, which makes him nearly unmovable and nearly impossible to circle. He has no reserve and no second state: he does one thing at the speed of a furnace and then he is carrying, because carrying is the job.
strengths: too dense to be shifted by anything the face can field, so he holds a line by standing on it
fast enough to close a distance that the mineral half should not be able to cross
cannot be knocked down, thrown, or made to give ground by a body the frame would license
no reserve means nothing about him is worth taking, so a lost exchange costs him nothing he was saving
weaknesses: has no room for a reserve at all, so he cannot spend twice in one engagement
the yin-organ gate is shut in him permanently, and no technique opens a second organ
has sixty years and the line he carries has three hundred and fifty, so he is the short half of his own inheritance
cannot be repaired in the field for a mineral fracture and burns for the fire one, so an injury is an appointment
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to move him and do not wait for a second exchange. Everything he does arrives once and at the speed of a furnace body, and the frame he is built on cannot hold a reserve to do it twice. Bring weight you can spare and be somewhere flat, because the only thing that reliably beats a body this dense is a frame that can inscribe what it is made of, and nothing on the plains can.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him at the assay floor, because the floor publishes measured stone before any sale and publishes no body that worked it.
The guild's lease register records four holders of his face in eleven years and does not record why three of them are not re-signing.

art.palette_notes: Quarry indigo-black and ash grey carry nearly the whole value range, with two accents: the heat flush at the collarbone and the raw ochre assay chip at his belt. Light is drawn half emitted and half absorbed — a warm internal line low in the chest that never fully lights the frame around it, so the darkest values sit inside his silhouette. Ink contours very heavy on the outline, the mineral seam on the forearm drawn as a fracture line that catches light rather than as a mark.

identity.realm: Fourteenth gate, stopped there on a body's own account, because the seventeenth is where the densest bodies stop and she would rather be refused honestly than be one of the ones who cannot come back

appearance.presentation: A mortuary clerk who reads as a lamp because she stands in doorways. That is not vanity: a Lanternfolk at the threshold of a room is legible as a light source, and the mortuary college has spent four generations turning that legibility into a credential nobody checks, which is the only office she can actually hold here.
appearance.age: Fifty-one. The Lanternfolk span runs to a little under sixty, which puts her in the last sixth of a life she has spent entirely inside other people's doors, and she has arranged her work so that the last sixth is the part nobody can reassign.
appearance.build: Narrow, upright, and slightly cold-looking, with the fixed carriage of somebody who stands in a doorway for a living and has made standing a profession.
appearance.complexion: Warm brown with the fine shadow of someone who works at the edges of lamplight and therefore is always lit from one side, and a paleness at the knuckles from cold stone thresholds.
appearance.hair: Dark shot through early with grey, pinned up in the college's fashion and coming loose at the temple on the side that faces the lamp, which is the side she is always standing on.
appearance.eyes: Amber and very steady, with pupils that contract early and hold, which is a body reading a dark room and is not a trick.
appearance.palette: College grey-brown and lamp ochre carry everything, with one saturated accent that is not worn but carried: a shuttered lantern clipped at her hip that is lit whenever she is indoors and dark whenever she is under a sky.
appearance.attire: College grey over a high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and thick-soled shoes for stone thresholds; the lantern at her hip is heavy and warm and she has never once been asked to put it down, because the college's whole method is that the light belongs to the office.
appearance.marks: A burn on the inside of her left wrist from a lamp in an accident she has never written up, and the pale indent of a pin worn for thirty years at the same point of the same temple.
appearance.bearing: Still in the middle of a doorway and never in the middle of a room, and she can turn to face either side without her light changing which side of a face it is on.

canon.role_in_story: Three Auditors of Tributes may sit at once and the fourth is refused on capacity, which is a different refusal from a single seat's occupied and produces a different situation for whoever is refused. Iselde is the fourth. The Field Registry keeps the burnt list — at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers — and an audit nobody can replace is a private accounting rather than an office. She holds the audit of who draws upkeep from the vacant seats, and is the person who must certify that nothing was taken, which is only worth doing if taking was once attempted.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the mortuary chapel doorway with the lantern lit, reading the assembly of a funeral over the heads of the mourners, and being asked by the registrar to state which of them the frame said rather than which of them the village remembered.
canon.lore: The Lanternfolk are a body solved for the dark: a hundred-year species that is legible at a distance and legible specifically as a light, and a culture — the door liturgy — built on the fact that a threshold is the edge of a law budget and the world will not promise welcome. The mortuary college's method descends directly from that: you stand in the doorway, you are the light, and whatever is in the room is read by it. A great ascension leaves debris and a record, so the culture keeps no temple and no museum; it keeps a register, and the register is the only relic.
history: Raised at the Hearth Common on the third layer, where a common concentration is the setting's most ordinary inheritance and its grant is small on purpose.
Taken into the Field Registry at nineteen as a doorway reader, the job the college gives to nobody with a cultivation path, on the grounds that a light should not be able to run an examination.

Discovered at thirty-one that the college's cases accumulate — one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body — and that the ambiguity is the college's standing revenue.

Appointed Auditor of Tributes at forty and immediately became the fourth, which is refused on capacity rather than on occupancy, a distinction the office's whole authority depends on and which nobody outside the registry can state.
Began keeping the fourth seat's paper in a form the fifth auditor could read, on the reasoning that a refusal on capacity is only defensible if the person refused can see what was refused over.

personality.summary: Cool, precise, and privately certain that the registry's ambiguity is a business rather than a failure. She is a woman who audits the drawing of upkeep from seats that do not exist, which makes her the administrator of a question she is also the beneficiary of, and she has never been able to find a way to hold the two apart.
traits: reads a room by its light and a person by what the frame says about them, in that order
refuses on capacity rather than on occupancy, and insists on the difference in every setting
keeps exact figures and exact dates and quotes both, which is her entire leverage
cannot be relieved, because the fourth seat cannot be vacated, only declined
mannerisms: turns to face a door whenever she decides to answer a question
lifts the lantern a hand's width before she enters a room and lowers it before she leaves
cites the case number and the year together, in that order
stops writing when the registrar enters, which the registrar has learned to read as an answer
motivations: wants the fourth seat's paper published so that the capacity refusal can be appealed rather than merely obeyed
wants the sealed cases opened by somebody with standing outside the registry, and has no idea who that would be
wants the ledger of vacant-seat upkeep to name a payer, which the notary would then have to certify, and knows that naming one would repay it
wants to be relieved, and has begun trying to make the fourth seat refuse her
flaws: has decided that the registry's revenue is a legitimate arrangement rather than an evasion, and defends it in arguments she does not believe
keeps the only record of the upkeep question, which is the question she administers, which is the problem she has spent nineteen years documenting
cannot separate her reading of a frame from her reading of the people in the room, and has been wrong about a person exactly once
treats the fourth seat as a kind of immortality and has not noticed that a seat which cannot be vacated cannot be left either
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and colder than the room. Says capacity and occupancy as if they were two different countries. Gives dates. Always dates, and always the year before the case number. One observation about the difference between a vacancy and an absence, made once, in a registry, years ago.
taboos: will not certify a death she has not been permitted to examine, and has left four open rather than break it
will not draw upkeep from a vacant seat, whatever the ledger shows, and has refused twice
will not answer a question from the chapel floor with the lantern lit, because a lit lamp in a doorway is a reading and a reading is a record
will not let the fourth seat be filled behind her by any means, including her own resignation

relationships.note: The college keeps the burnt list, reading the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, because realm nine was a limit nobody was issued, so the record of a life is also the record of a gate that was never available to it. It keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify and the cases accumulate, which makes the ambiguity its standing revenue and makes her the officer who certifies it.

Three Auditors may sit at once and the fourth is refused on capacity, which is a different refusal from a seat's being occupied and produces a different situation for whoever is refused. She is the standing example of that difference: an audit nobody can replace is a private accounting rather than an office, and hers is an audit nobody may vacate either.

Unclaimed capacity is the only thing that pays its own upkeep, so an unfilled seat is described as funding the tier it sits in, and something is drawing from it on the same closed budget everything else competes to hold. The notary certifies a seat empty and is the body that would have to say where the payment went, so the question is administered by its own beneficiary, which is her office.

The college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because the frames keep producing the record without the body. She pays for the seals and charges for the files, so the ambiguity pays for itself and nobody can call it a failure without closing the column.

A fire-affinity culture's full ritual of the broken ceiling keeps an unbroken shell, the whole recovery recorded publicly, and the fragments never displayed again, because a great ascension is a body opened on a purpose. It has no temples and no museum; it has a register, and the register is the only relic it keeps — which is the entire institutional logic of the mortuary college she audits.

That office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because four vacant seats were very nearly filled by decree and the attempt taught the setting to write a vacancy as its own state rather than as a zero. Her registry certifies that nothing was taken from those seats, which is only worth doing if taking was once attempted, and the notary is the office that would have to admit it.

The lodge sells bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, on the ground that a boundary is the edge of a law budget and a body arriving where a required group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed. It is the only institution in the setting whose charter has a place for a person the tier cannot produce, and she has read its terms and has not applied.

reference_stats.summary: Almost no offensive capacity and the ability to make any fight irrelevant, because she can read the frame a thing is happening in before it resolves. Everything she wins, she wins by being the person holding the light, which means it depends entirely on being the one in the doorway.
strengths: reads a room's law state from the doorway before entering it, so she is never surprised by a frame
steady under lamplight in a way that makes her the best witness any registrar could want
holds four hundred sealed cases and every date on them, which is leverage nobody else in the setting can match
cannot be intimidated, flattered, or hurried, because her authority is a rule about numbers and not about her
weaknesses: has no offensive practice at all, and depends absolutely on there being a room she is standing in
cannot be relieved, replaced, or refused an audience, which means she is trapped in exactly the way she is documenting
the fourth seat is refused on capacity rather than vacated, so her position can be ended by nobody including her
her own audit is the record of a question she administers, which makes every finding she publishes an admission
reference_stats.combat_read: Never enter a room she is standing in. Her advantage is positional and entirely about the frame, not about her, so take her out of the frame: cross a threshold she has not opened, put her somewhere with no doorway, or bring something the frame cannot read and therefore cannot be entered by a light. She cannot win an exchange and does not need to; she only has to keep the light on.
notes: The college quotes no stat line for her, because an auditor is entered in the register as a seat and a seat has no body attached to it.
She has never been recorded as being in the fourth seat. She has been recorded four times as being refused it, and the four refusals are the only evidence that the seat exists.

identity.realm: Eighth gate, the last of the ordinary meridians, and there is no body left to close the girdling vessel in — a four-legged frame carries its mass on the forelimbs and has no hindquarter girth, so it reaches the liver gate and stops

appearance.presentation: An animal on a ledger. He reads as a very large ash-belt scavenger that somebody has taught to hold a stylus, and the Watch has had to write a policy about whether that makes him a soldier, which it does, and the policy is longer than his service record.
appearance.age: Nine seasons by his own count, which is a young adult for a pack quadruped and an implausible span for anybody who has read a contract, and the Watch records him by season rather than by year for exactly that reason.
appearance.build: Long, low and dark, standing about a head above a kneeling clerk, with the deep chest and heavy forequarters of a frame built to arrive after everybody else has left.
appearance.complexion: Charcoal-black with the ash-dust ground into the coat along the spine, and a paler underside where the belt grit has never settled, which is the only part of him that reads as clean.
appearance.hair: Not hair — a coarse guard-hair along the spine that stands up when he is reading a gradient and lies flat when he is content, and the Watch quartermaster has learned to use that as an early warning and has never told him.
appearance.eyes: Amber and unblinking, set wide and slightly forward, with a permanent narrowed squint from the ash belt that he brought with him and has never fully recovered from.
appearance.palette: Ninth Watch slate on a harness cut for a body with four weight-bearing points, with one accent that is belt-yellow at the throat strap and one that is entirely not clothing: the ash-dust in the guard-hair, which is lighter than anything else in the frame.
appearance.attire: A slate harness cut for a quadruped's shoulders, four buckles at the points that carry load, and a slate satchel slung under the chest where a ledger rides. The harness is issued, the ledger is his, and the distinction is the only part of the arrangement he has been told about.
appearance.marks: A healed tear through one ear, and a slate-dust tattoo on the inside of the near foreleg where the guild marks a working animal that has been taught something.
appearance.bearing: Low, forward and constantly moving in small circles at the edge of whatever it has decided is the important part of a room.

canon.role_in_story: The Ninth Watch is the only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair, and its one doctrine is that a queue of bodies is the one thing that must not become a fight. Corvin is the Watch's residue reader: a scavenger that reads the qi a thing leaves behind, posted at the one door where arrivals are continuous and unrecorded. His use is enormous and his status is a policy problem, because the setting's law treats a pack as a kinship by scent and not as a polity, and the Watch wrote a longer document about him than about any of its own officers.
canon.first_appearance: First seen circling a clerk's tent at the foot of the stair, stopped dead facing the tent's rear wall, and refusing to move when the clerk came out to ask what he wanted.
canon.lore: A pack quadruped that eats what qi leaves behind. Death on the ash belt is frequent, unattended and rich, so a predator that cannot win a fight is not a predator here — it is a scavenger, and the scavenger niche is not thin but permanent. The ashjackal is built for it: fast, unspecialised, able to read a qi gradient through falling ash from far enough away to arrive after everyone else has left. What it costs is everything that requires standing still. They cannot take a healthy adult of anything, which is why they are removed from a live fight in under a minute, and they are the clearest example in the setting of a life built entirely around not being present.
history: Born in a pack on the ash belt that dissolved twice inside a season and reformed three times, which is a foraging strategy and not a family and which taught him that a group is a thing that ends.
Fed on a corpse at a settlement that did not know its dead were being read and eaten, and established that a carcass's residual qi is legible for about a day and a half to anything shaped like him.
Brought to the foot of the stair by a Watch quartermaster who had lost a man to an unlicensed arrival and wanted the arrivals read before they reached the gate.
Given a satchel, a ledger and a post, and discovered within a season that the ledger is the only part of the arrangement that is harder than scavenging.

Taught by the gate clerks to circle rather than rush, because he would clear the queue faster than he could ever be removed from a live fight, and the clerks have not yet decided whether this is training or a description.

personality.summary: Focused, busy, and entirely without the concept of a queue, which is the single most quartermasterly thing about him and the reason he is the best residue reader the Watch has. He is not loyal in a way a person would recognise; he is oriented, the way a compass is oriented, and he reads a room as a gradient.
traits: reads residual qi as a direction and cannot be taught to read it as anything else
refuses to be still for more than a few seconds and does not understand why this is a problem
is not attached to any individual and is entirely consistent about it
knows the gate better than the officers do and is not permitted to say so
mannerisms: circles the thing he is interested in, low and slow, with his head down
stops dead and points his whole body when he reads a gradient
makes a low chuff at the Watch quartermaster and nothing at anybody else
will not cross a threshold he has read as cold, and has refused four gate crossings on that basis
motivations: wants the ledger finished before the shift ends, which is the only want he has ever been asked to hold and the only one he keeps
wants to be permitted to the gate floor rather than the tent, where the readings are actually useful
wants the stall that is a person rather than a gradient to be recognised as a thing worth reading, and has reported it eleven times
wants to be read correctly rather than quickly, having worked out that the officers write both
flaws: cannot be made to wait, and the gate's only function is waiting, so his usefulness and his posting are in permanent conflict
has learned that being useful is what earns him a post and has stopped distinguishing useful from permitted
does not understand exclusion and cannot be taught it, so he has no idea that the tent is a lesser place
takes any order that points at a gradient, which is a very short chain to an order he should refuse
personality.voice: Not speech. Three sounds, all of them short: a chuff for the quartermaster, a rising note for a gradient, and a single flat note he uses when somebody has asked him to stop and he has not. The clerks have written all three into the policy. The flat note is described in the policy as an objection, which is the most generous reading anybody has given it. The rising note is the only sound he makes at the gate itself.
taboos: will not cross a threshold he has read as cold, and has refused four crossings
will not enter a live fight, which he cannot help and which the policy documents as a limitation of the species
will not eat anything inside a building, a rule the belt taught him and the Watch has had to write down
will not be called a soldier to his face, and the flat note is the answer

relationships.note: The only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair, because the only door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter it fills with unlicensed arrivals. It needs something that can read an arrival before it becomes a queue, and it has written a longer policy about what he is than about any of its own officers, which is the shape the problem has taken.

A pack is a kinship by scent and dissolves when the scent changes, so it is a foraging strategy that happens to have members and not a polity or a social form. He has been taught to stay, which is the one thing the strategy cannot do, and the teaching has cost him every advantage the design gave him.

That guild exists because waste does not disperse on a frame with no spatial law, and it pays the only genuinely scarce labour on the tier. He would be cheaper and more useful on the heap than at the gate, and the Watch has had this offer twice and refused it both times because a gate that cannot be read is a fight waiting for a queue.

A levy company is paid per name and keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor were recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. His ledger records arrivals rather than names, and he writes the entries in the same shape, and nobody has ever compared the two columns.

One region carries two incompatible reckonings and which calendar a contract is written in decides whether it can be disputed at all. He cannot be given either, so his readings are recorded as a direction and an interval, which is not a figure and is the only entry in the gate ledger that cannot be falsified by a clerk with a different calendar.

The children of the levy are called, fed, trained and entered nowhere, because the March may call a levy and may not own a body. He is on a roster by season and not by year, which is the same arrangement applied to a species nobody agreed to raise.

reference_stats.summary: No fight at all and the finest approach warning in the setting. He cannot take a healthy adult of anything and is removed from a live engagement in under a minute, which means every exchange he wins is won before it starts, by arriving after everybody else has left.
strengths: reads a residual qi gradient through falling ash from far enough away to arrive after everyone is gone
absorbs residual qi out of ash and carcass faster than anything else measured, so a battlefield feeds him
fast and unspecialised, with no technique to learn and no stance to be read in
cannot be threatened, frightened, or bribed by anything a technique can do, because techniques are what his kind eats
weaknesses: cannot take a healthy adult of anything, so any fight that reaches contact removes him from it
requires everything that requires standing still, and standing still is what a queue is made of
a four-legged frame reaches the eighth gate and then has no hindquarter girth to close the girdling vessel against
is posted to the one place he must not be able to leave, on a form that names him by season rather than by name
reference_stats.combat_read: Never fight him — arrive late. Everything he gives you is information that cost him nothing to find and everything to stay for. His whole design is a life built around not being present, so the only approach that reaches him is a slow one that keeps him in contact longer than a minute, which is a discipline for the opponent and not for him. Anything that kills the last thing on the field is simply his next meal.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him in the Watch ledger, because the ledger has a season column and a direction column and no column for what he is.
The Watch has never established whether the flat note is a word. The policy says it is an objection and the quartermaster says it is his name.

art.palette_notes: Ninth Watch slate on a charcoal frame, with the ash-dust in the guard-hair drawn as a pale grey that is lighter than anything else in the picture and is the only thing giving his top edge against a dark ground. The belt-yellow throat strap is the single saturated accent. Light is drawn as low and raking, catching the spine guard-hair so that his silhouette reads as a line of pale ash over black. Ink contours heavy at the forequarters and dissolving at the tail.

identity.realm: Sixth gate, and structurally sixth for life: a body path that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain closes at the same place it opens them, so the discipline that makes a threshold-builder good at walls makes the same person impossible above the sixth

appearance.presentation: A woman built like a doorframe and dressed like one: squared shoulders, a spine that has been corrected twice by a craft rather than by a fight, and the heavy hands of somebody who measures by eye because measuring by instrument does not work on this ground. The ridge reads her as staff before it reads her as a person, because the pass keepers do.
appearance.age: Thirty-eight. A stonebound's sixty years is the most durable crossing the setting can build and two thirds short of the mineral line it carries, so she has been treating herself as borrowed since she was old enough to be told.
appearance.build: Square and heavy, thick through the shoulder blades from carrying a beam rather than a load, and standing with her weight exactly on the join between two thresholds out of a habit nobody trained into her.
appearance.complexion: Pale grey-flecked stone with the surface sheen of something that has been in cold wind for a decade, and a permanent warm flush along the throat where the mineral half has nowhere to put what the fire half makes.
appearance.hair: Dark and coarse, cut brutally short because anything else catches on a lintel, and grey at the temple on the side that faces the pass wind.
appearance.eyes: Grey and very still, narrowed against glare, with the internal heat visible only when she is looking down into a chamber.
appearance.palette: Slate and mortared grey carry almost everything, with one saturated accent — the Jade Writ's waxed green on the band she wears at the throat — and one structural accent: a chalk line across the sill behind her, which is the colour of the mark she is there to renew.
appearance.attire: Threshold grey over boiled hide, cut close at the neck so nothing snags, with a chalk pouch and a steel rule she does not use because the ground will not hold an answer. Boots are the only warm thing she owns and they are replaced every year.
appearance.marks: A lintel bruise across one shoulder in the exact place a doorframe takes it, and a chalk line worn into the skin of her palm from four years of marking doorways.
appearance.bearing: Squared, planted and still, and she stands in doorways the way other people stand in rooms, which is the whole of her professional life in one habit.

canon.role_in_story: The Jade Writ collects debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the Sixfold Ridge, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person, nobody may levy a seat, and somebody therefore has to decide who is owed the gate. Between the office and the ground sits a smaller job nobody has ever named: the Writ marks its own thresholds, because a world boundary is the edge of a law budget and the frame under a pass changes without announcing it. Tamsyne holds that job on a term that rotates, which means nobody is ever in post long enough to notice that the mark has stopped matching the door.
canon.lore: An unwritten law is not a weak law but an absent one, with no dial and nothing to push, so a community needing a guarantee of welcome cannot get one from the world and has to mark it itself. That practice is the door liturgy, and the builders' guild that inherits it takes as its measure that what it builds is tested from the other side. The whole institution rests on a contradiction the setting never resolves: a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not, and nobody on the pass has the standing to say which of the two has moved.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at a sill below the pass with the coat off and the Writ's chalk in her hand, already on her third mark of the morning when the clerk who had renewed it came down to ask why she was doing it again.
history: Born into the second house on the ridge, which holds the pass ground while the calendar sits with the reeves, and grew up on the standing agreement that the two houses argue only about price.

Taken on at sixteen as a marker's apprentice on the building guild, taught the craft in a body that was never designed to take the meridian burn a qi technique uses, and discovered in the third year that hardening bone closes what the meridian needs open.

Given the Writ's rotating term at twenty-six after the previous clerk put down the chalk and would not take it back, on the grounds that a person who has marked a threshold for four years can no longer see it.

Began keeping her own record of which marks had been renewed on which date and against which reading of the ground, and found on the third season that the Writ's own record disagreed with hers in eleven places.
Went back over every mark on the ridge below the pass, unasked, in one winter, and found two that had been renewed by a clerk who had never been issued the Writ's chalk.

personality.summary: Exact, unsentimental, and privately certain that a rotating term is a way of not having to decide anything. She is a woman whose craft is honest and whose office is not, and she has spent four winters assembling the evidence that would let somebody else say so, which is the only form of protest available to a clerk on a term.
traits: reads a joint by sound before she looks at it, which the builders' craft taught her and the office never asked her to use
keeps her own record against the office's and has never once shown it to the office
will not mark a threshold she has not stood in twice, and this has cost her two promotions
is precise about what she knows and refuses to generalise, which makes her useless at her own job
mannerisms: stands in the join of a doorway rather than the flat of it, without appearing to notice
taps the sill once with a knuckle before writing anything on it
takes her coat off to mark a threshold and puts it back on to argue about the mark
answers a question about a date with a date and a question about a mark with a joint
motivations: wants the eleven disagreements between her record and the Writ's produced in open, and has now twice been told to file them
wants the term lengthened to the life of a mark, on the grounds that a mark renewed by nobody is not a mark
wants to be the clerk who found the two unauthorized renewals rather than the clerk who quietly redid them
wants to be told that re-marking the whole ridge in one winter was the correct use of a term she was not supposed to have
flaws: has decided that careful record-keeping is the same as pressure and has not yet discovered that a record nobody is shown is not pressure at all
cannot generalise, so four winters of her own record has not become one complaint and may never become one
stays in posts she knows are wrong because leaving is a decision she has not authorised herself to make
treats the office as the problem and the people in it as colleagues, which has kept her from the only thing that would have worked
personality.voice: Flat and technical, and much more precise about stone than about people. Names a joint by what it is doing rather than by where it is, because that is how she finds it. One question she asks every office that hires her, and she asked it here too: who renewed this, and when.
taboos: will not mark a threshold she has not stood in twice
will not renew a mark she has not chalked herself, whatever the office's record says
will not leave a mark that no one maintains without writing that down beside it
will not sign the Writ's record as agreeing with her own

relationships.note: The office collects debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the ridge, because nobody may levy a seat and somebody has to decide who is owed the gate. It marks its own thresholds because the frame under a pass changes without announcing itself, and it does that with a clerk on a term that rotates, which means the mark is renewed by somebody who has not yet noticed it stopped matching the door.

A house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame under it changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not, because an unwritten law has no dial and nothing to push. She does the whole practice and has written down, in her own record, eleven cases where the mark and the frame had stopped agreeing.

That guild builds and then guards doors, walls and thresholds, and takes as its measure that what it builds is tested from the other side, because the frame's borders have to be held by somebody with an interest in them being impassable. The guild paid for a second and shorter ladder in its own currency because the same density that lets a body carry and lift closes what a qi technique needs open.

A guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn a qi path uses. She is the product of that bargain and is living inside its exact terms: better than anyone at carrying a lintel, permanently short of anything above the sixth gate.

The second house on the ridge holds the pass ground while the calendar sits with the reeves, because a family holding both the ground and the schedule would be uninsailable, so the ground was given away deliberately. She has offered the eleven disagreements to both houses and the second house's answer was to ask who had renewed the mark, which is a question about ground rather than about the office.

One region, two incompatible reckonings, and which calendar a contract is written in decides whether it can be disputed at all. She keeps her renewal dates against a flood post rather than a day-count, which is the half of the calendar nobody can inflate, and it is the reason her record and the office's disagree on eleven marks without either being wrong.

The other half of the Peak Ascent absence, holding the crop the absent left a claim to instead of the absent's name, because a household with no cultivator still has an estate and grain is the only thing anybody will accept as payment for a crossing. It is her father's household, it has no cultivator in it now, and the pass gate is the only place its standing can be spent.

reference_stats.summary: A body built to carry and to hold, with a discipline that hardens her against exactly the strain she is standing in. She does not have a reserve and does not have a second state either; everything she has is in the frame and the frame has been closed against the next four gates.
strengths: reads a joint by sound before it fails, which in a building is the difference between a repair and a collapse
cannot be moved, thrown, or frightened, and will not leave a post she is standing in
heavier and denser than anything the pass can field, so she holds a sill alone
no reserve means nothing about her is worth taking
weaknesses: closed at the sixth gate by her own craft, permanently, and no technique opens a meridian that hardening has closed
carries stone better than she carries anything alive, which is a fault exactly where a boundary needs defending
has no offensive practice and would rather repair than engage
is posted on a rotating term, so her competence compounds and resets roughly every three years
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her on a floor she has stood on twice. Everything she has is in the frame, and the frame is only hers where she has already read the joint. Put her somewhere the ground is new: she becomes an ordinary heavy body on ground she has not tested, and the read-by-sound advantage — which is most of what she is — simply stops applying.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her by the Writ, because the office records who renewed a mark and not what the person holding the chalk could do.
Her own record of renewal dates is four winters long and has been shown to exactly one person, who was a clerk's widow and told her it was the most careful thing she had ever seen.

art.palette_notes: Slate and mortared grey carry nearly the whole value range, with two accents: the waxed green of the Writ at her throat and the chalk white of a renewed mark, which is the only true white in the picture and is always a line. Light is drawn as cold daylight against cold stone, hard and almost shadowless because the pass is above cloud, and the internal heat at her throat is the single warm note in an otherwise grey frame. Ink contours very heavy on the shoulders and the lintel line, everything else thin.

identity.realm: Fourth gate and no further. The yin-organ gate needs a channel running between distinct pairs of organs, and a rootmarch's three sap columns branch but do not pair, so it stops where the pairing starts and everything above it is anatomically false

appearance.presentation: A student seated in a place rather than sitting in it. She occupies a field the school has had fenced for eleven years and is read as part of the school's grounds — a bench with a canopy, a reading frame, a very slow face — and the difficulty is that from four hundred paces this is indistinguishable from the school's furniture.
appearance.age: Twenty-six seasons of root. A rootmarch fruit drops in soil it can root into and cannot move once it has, so her age is a date in a ledger and not a number she carries, and the school records the year she established and has never asked since.
appearance.build: Rooted and upright, wooden through the lower trunk with a human chest above it and a bark-scaled collar where the two meet, and long arms with three-jointed hands built for breaking a soil crust rather than for turning a page.
appearance.complexion: Pale bark over the limbs, a warm ochre flush through the chest where the sap runs, and a faint bloom of soil on the shoulders that no amount of grooming removes because it is in the bark, not on it.
appearance.hair: A crown of leaf-dark growth that changes with the season and cannot be cut without costing her a season's vigour, so the school leaves it alone and has had to write that down.
appearance.eyes: Amber and slow, focused a long way off, with a fixed way of turning to follow a speaker that takes longer than a person's patience and is not rudeness.
appearance.palette: Gap School's chalk-white and dark green carry everything, with the only saturated accent being the ochre of a fruit still attached at her hip — the seed that produced her, kept in a frame because throwing it would be the only way to travel.
appearance.attire: A reading frame of lacquered cane and cloth slung on a hook frame that travels on a bar and does not lift her, high-collared and long-sleeved, and a soil apron at the base of the trunk where the ground meets wood. Nothing about her is armour and everything about her is a plant's answer to the problem of being a person.
appearance.marks: A healed graft scar at the left shoulder where a limb was pruned and re-broke, and the pale seam of the fruit's attachment scar at her hip.
appearance.bearing: Immobile and unhurried in the way a growing thing is unhurried, with the canopy of her crown turning toward whatever is warm and away from whoever is asking.

canon.role_in_story: The Gap School teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and then moving the student somewhere that law is missing. A spare seat is not capacity for a new path; it is the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed. Every candidate in that method has to leave, and Sela is the school's standing demonstration of the one case that cannot, which is why a farm organism with no root in soil and no way to move is being examined here at all.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the school's fenced lower field at the hour a class was scheduled to move somewhere else, still in the ground she was seated in, while the rest of the class was being counted twice on the way out.
canon.lore: Every other body in this setting stores wealth in muscle, in qi, or in a colony. A rootmarch stores it in seed, and seed survives a famine that kills a grain store, which is the whole reason: a plant lineage is the only one in the record that holds a harvest across the bad years. The trade is total. Wood is not muscle, there is no tissue to temper, and the body path is closed outright. The ceiling is the fourth gate, because the yin-organ gate needs a channel between distinct pairs of organs and a rootmarch's three sap columns branch without pairing.
history: Fruited in a cleft household's field as a seed stock and rooted in the third season, which is the dangerous part of a rootmarch life: establishment, not conception.
Was examined by the household at the fourth gate, told the gate is shut rather than unmet, and rooted further into the same ground over the next two seasons as though the news were about the weather.
Carried up the stair on a bar and a hook frame by a household that had decided to see whether the setting's arithmetic held, and established in the school's lower field within a month of arrival.

Became the school's first seated difference in the fourth season, when the diff showed that the gate she stopped at was not a shortage of anything but a shortage of pairing, and the finding was in the school's favour for exactly one term.
Has been offered a second seating three times and refused it each time in writing, on the grounds that the fruit at her hip is the only ticket she has and the school has no chamber that can be moved.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that reads as slow and is in fact a completely different thing: she is on a schedule measured in seasons rather than hours and has no mechanism for hurrying. She is also the only person at the school who can be certain about one result, because she is the result.
traits: answers on a delay that is not hesitation and will not be hurried out of it
knows the school's method better than most of its teachers and has never been allowed to teach it
treats the ground she is in as a document and the season as a clock, which is a school habit she did not have to be taught
refuses things in writing, which she learned from watching an institution and now uses against it
mannerisms: turns the crown toward warmth rather than toward whoever is speaking
touches the fruit at her hip when she is about to refuse something
answers a question by naming the season and the growth stage rather than by naming a person
goes silent for a full season-length pause and then answers completely
motivations: wants the fourth-gate finding published as an anatomy result rather than as a failure of supply, because it is the only fact the school has that survives its own closure
wants to be examined in a frame that has spatial law seated, and has been told twice that the school cannot afford one
wants the fruit carried to soil rather than framed, and cannot ask for it without asking to leave
wants somebody to sit with her for a full season without asking her to be faster
flaws: has decided that patience is a position rather than a limitation, and the school has taught her that by never contradicting her
cannot leave, so every objection she has is an objection she will be sitting in when she makes it
has let the school's method become her own, which means she now thinks like the thing she is evidence about
knows her own ceiling precisely and has begun to find that knowledge restful, which is the most dangerous thing in her record
personality.voice: Slow, exact, and entirely without impatience, because she does not experience the timescale on which other people hurry her. Names things by their stage of growth rather than by their use, and has to translate for people at speed. One complaint, about being examined, delivered in a season and repeated every season since.
taboos: will not be seated somewhere she cannot establish, which is every place
will not be described as a plant, and will correct the description politely and at length
will not throw the fruit, which is the only journey available to her
will not be asked to be faster and has never once pretended to try

relationships.note: The school teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits and moving the student somewhere that law is missing, because a spare seat is the only condition under which a law can be studied rather than obeyed. She is the standing demonstration that the fourth gate is shut for want of pairing rather than for want of anything, which is the one finding the school has that cannot be copied by anybody else on the grounds.

The fourth body realm is the last one before the gate that asks for heart, small intestine, bladder and kidney as distinct structures with a channel between each pair, and that gate is not a supply problem. She clears the gate set on stored sap alone and stops, and being told that ascending past the fourth is anatomically false is the single fact her whole life is organised around.

That house holds no jade and owns the workings anyway, because jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so whoever provisions the cutters owns the cleft more durably than whoever digs it. She fruited in its field as stock, which is what a household that cannot farm its own ground does with a body that will not leave it.

Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures a body rather than slowing it, and it is a licensed experiment at this academy and a capital offence everywhere else. The experiment they tried on her was spatial, on the theory that a rooted body could be taught to establish elsewhere, and the failure is what confirmed the ceiling.

The jade cleft's draft is the only place a rootmarch can hold a season of sap, because jade holds qi and will not give it up and the surrounding workings are thin, hard and increasingly deep. She is standing in the only soil on that tier that will feed her, which is why the school fenced a field rather than moving her.

Mortals on this tier set a broken limb by hand with the same method for a century and never improve it, because improving it costs iron and iron here is consumed by clearing spoil. Pruning and re-breaking is what happens to her instead, and it costs a season's vigour rather than a piece of worked metal, which is the one place the tier's economy is gentler on her than on a person.

A fire-affinity house signs every child to a furnace before it is named, because the body has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve. Her household did the same operation with seed: establish before you are named, and you cannot be moved afterwards. Both lineages inherit by attaching and neither can be freed, and the two have never met to compare notes.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight and has not been asked to. What she has is the ability to seal in a dark field and live for months, which in a famine makes her the most valuable thing in the region and in a war makes her a hostage who cannot refuse. Everything she is good at is a form of staying.
strengths: survives sealed in the dark for months without water, movement or conversation, which nothing else on the tier can do
cannot be hurried, flanked, or frightened, because none of those are operations a rooted body supports
has no reserve to spend and nothing worth stealing, so a raid costs her season rather than life
in a famine she outlasts every mobile body in the region, and she knows it
weaknesses: cannot move once rooted, so she is a fixture and every plan that includes her has to be a plan that comes to her
no tissue to temper, so the body path is closed outright and every attempt disperses rather than fails
no heart and no kidney analogue, so there is no channel to close and the fourth gate is a permanent wall
cannot be rescued from anywhere she does not want to be, which makes her cooperation the only variable in her own situation
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange available. A rooted body that cannot move and cannot fight is not a combatant, so the only approach is to make the situation urgent and hope she treats urgency as weather — which she will not. Bring siege rather than a strike, and remember that the fastest way to lose a siege is to give her a reason to stay: destroying her ground is the only blow that lands, and it takes a season she does not have to hurry.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her anywhere, because the school records her as a seated difference and a seated difference is a location, which the register has one line for and no body attached to it.
Her own record of the fourth-gate finding is the only document in the school that describes her ceiling as anatomy, and it is kept on the frame above her head where she can read it.

art.palette_notes: Chalk-white and dark green carry the school, with the single saturated accent being the ochre of the fruit still attached at her hip — the only warm object in the picture and the only thing in it that is going anywhere. Light is drawn as two sources: cold high-altitude daylight from above, and a faint ochre glow from the sap moving in her chest, so the two never quite agree. Ink contours heavy on the bark at the base and dissolving into leaf-dry line at the crown.

identity.realm: Nothing. A deepsalt's whole existence is a trade: the brine is a substrate rather than a habitat, and nothing in the record contains a gate above the floor it stands in

appearance.presentation: A broker's assessor who cannot leave the isle he assesses, and who has therefore become the isle's most reliable fixture and the firm's least mobile asset. He reads as a large pale man standing very still in brine, which on this isle is a professional qualification rather than an inconvenience.
appearance.age: Eighty-one seasons. The saltfolk parent runs to a long service life and the subspecies is slower on top of that, so he has been on the isle for sixty years and has a documented case for why he could not have left before the fortieth.
appearance.build: Broad, thick and slow, with the heavy shoulders and dense frame of a body designed to live under several feet of saturated brine rather than to move through it.
appearance.complexion: Pale grey with a mineral sheen and a white salt bloom along the forearms and collar, and the brine-dark line at the jaw that never quite dries.
appearance.hair: White, thin and flattened, and permanently wet at the ends from the basin standing a hand's depth in every room on the isle.
appearance.eyes: Pale and slightly rolled, adapted to reading light through brine, and they close almost completely when he is thinking, which the firm has learned to read as a refusal forming.
appearance.palette: Firm indigo and the isle's bone white carry everything, with one saturated accent — a jade assay chip at his throat on a cord — and the brine itself is drawn as a second light source coming up from the floor.
appearance.attire: Firm indigo over a brine-proof apron cut for a body that never dries, high collar and long sleeves, and rubber-soled boots that are never taken off because taking them off is how a deepsalt discovers where the brine line is.
appearance.marks: Salt bloom across both forearms in a tide line that moves with the season, and a nail-thin scar across one cheek from the first year on the isle.
appearance.bearing: Very still and slightly downhill-leaning, the posture of a body that finds vertical effort expensive and has stopped apologising for it.

canon.role_in_story: The Salt Leech works the tailings on a dormant isle nobody collects from and sells the result as spirit stone, and it exists because a severed frame keeps paying upkeep nobody collects, and low-grade jade is worthless on the isle and unmatchable ashore. Its whole method requires somebody to stand on the floor and assess the seam by hand. Brennick is that somebody, and a subspecies that is a fixture of a basin and never a traveller is the only assessor the firm can rely on.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing ankle-deep in a drained cutting on the isle with both hands in the tailings, entirely still, and not answering the factor who had come down to ask him a question.
canon.lore: A deepsalt is the saltfolk of the basin floor, specialised past what the parent body could carry. They are a subspecies because a lineage was pushed onto a saturated floor whose brine layer is deep enough to hold a body in it permanently, and then kept there; every adaptation is the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down. Taken above the brine line it does not become ill, it stops, within hours. The parent has nine days. The subspecies has none worth counting.
history: Born to the parent saltfolk on the upper pan and taken down to the floor as a teenager by a broker who needed a body that would not sicken on the work, which was the first of several people to make that decision about her line.
Found the brine line at the age of nineteen by walking one step above it and having to be carried back down, which is the subspecies' whole biology stated as a single incident.

Been assessed at the floor and certified as the fastest cultivation rate of any saltfolk body, a result that could not be reproduced anywhere above the line and therefore could only be certified here.
Worked sixty seasons of tailings for four different firms, and stayed with this one through a change of hands that removed the assessment clause from his contract twice and reinstated it twice.

Refused, at seventy, a transfer to the mainland that would have paid four times the rate, on the grounds that a certified figure produced on the floor has never once been reproduced ashore and he is not willing to be the reason somebody assumed it was.

personality.summary: Slow in speech, slower in movement, and absolutely immovable on the substance. He is the most reliable assessor in the firm and the only one who cannot be replaced by somebody sent from ashore, which has given him a standing he never asked for and a decision he can never delegate.
traits: certifies a figure only where it can be reproduced, which has made him the only assessor the firm trusts and the only one who costs what he costs
takes his time in the way a body under several feet of brine takes its time and will not be hurried into a different shape
knows the isle's floor better than any record and has never written any of it down because he is not sure who would hold the paper
will not be moved off the floor, and has converted that from a limitation into a term of reference
mannerisms: closes his eyes almost fully when thinking and the firm reads that as a refusal forming
stands ankle-deep in brine while talking and does not appear to notice it
cites a figure by where it was taken rather than by what it was called
turns to face the seam rather than the person when a number is asked for
motivations: wants the floor's assessments carried ashore as certified rather than as copied, and has never been allowed to certify anything he cannot stand on
wants the firm's clause written back into his contract in a form that does not require him to argue for it every second season
wants to know whether the figures hold anywhere else, and has decided the only honest way to know is to leave, which he cannot do
wants somebody to take over the floor for one season so that he can be shown a figure he did not take
flaws: has turned being unable to leave into a professional identity and no longer distinguishes the two
certifies only what he stands on and has therefore made himself the bottleneck the firm blames for every delay

has never recorded anything, on the grounds that paper is evidence and evidence is leverage and leverage is how a house loses independence, which is a borrowed principle he has applied to his own work
believes the floor's figures are unique and would like that to be the reason he is valued rather than the reason he is trapped
personality.voice: Very slow and very level, with long pauses that are not hesitation and are better described as pressure. Gives a number only after saying where he took it, and refuses to give it at all if he cannot say where. One joke, about a mainland posting, delivered once and never repeated.
taboos: will not certify a figure he has not taken standing on the floor
will not be signed onto a mainland posting and has refused four
will not hand his floor notes to anybody ashore, on the grounds that a copy is not a certificate
will not be lifted out of the brine by anybody, whatever the reason given

relationships.note: The firm works tailings on a dormant isle nobody collects from because a severed frame keeps paying upkeep nobody collects, and low-grade jade is worthless on the isle and unmatchable ashore. Every figure it sells is a figure taken on the floor by a body that cannot leave the floor, so its most valuable asset is a man who has no other option and has begun to be proud of that.

The parent is the apex consumer of the most stable resource in the region, with triple renal mass and a hardened mineral crust, and it stalls at the eleventh gate because the brine sac that makes the body possible runs dorsal to the sternum and splits the penetrating vessel in two. The subspecies turns the same plan's tolerance up and its mobility down and inherits the same wall.

The measured quantity of stone left per unit of ground worked is published before any sale and never after, and it has been falling for three generations. He is the hand the disclosure is taken by, and he has never let a figure leave the isle without a statement of where it was taken, which is the whole of his professional ethics.

The conversion that lets anybody price anything across four tiers where time runs between half a hundred and a hundred times a mortal's works by never computing a rate, because passage is the setting's only accepted medium and it is denominated in a body. His assessment is denominated in a body that cannot pass, so the one instrument that would price his work cannot reach him.

The isle is either a piece cut from the shelf's floor when a seam was worked out from under it, or something shaped to look severed — and the challenger's account says its jade reads at a number no shore survey can match because it was never at the shore's number. He has produced four seasons of figures that match no shore survey and has been told this proves nothing in either direction.

If the isle was never part of the shelf, its jade reads at a number no shore survey can match because it was never at the shore's number, and its population are not a colony. Every figure he takes on the floor is a figure that cannot be checked against anything, and the broker who trades in removed imprints is the one party with a commercial reason to want that reading to hold.

A standing set of marriages between the counting houses and the underwriters is kept because the two could not merge: a merger would make one of them priceable, and a priceable counterparty can be bought. His assessments are what the underwriters write on, and the whole arrangement rests on nobody ever being able to price the floor.

reference_stats.summary: Fights badly and was never designed for it, and is close to unkillable on ground that has brine over it. Everything he can do happens at the pace of a body carrying several feet of liquid, and everything about him stops the moment he leaves that ground.
strengths: fastest cultivation rate of any saltfolk body, which is measurable only where the brine is deep enough to stand in
holds a brine substrate, so on the isle floor he does not tire, does not dehydrate, and does not need to
a saltfolk body is dependent on brine and reverses the entire relationship — anything trying to wash him off the floor is defeating itself
reads a seam by hand better than any instrument brought ashore, because the instruments cannot be calibrated there
weaknesses: stops within hours above the brine line rather than sickening, so removal is instant and total
cannot be moved, so he is a fixture and every firm change of hands is a change of employer he did not choose
has no cultivation gate above the floor he stands on and no technique that works anywhere else
cannot be replaced, which makes him valuable and means every delay on the isle is his fault
reference_stats.combat_read: Never bring him off the brine. A body whose whole biology runs on a substrate loses the moment the substrate thins, so the entire engagement is a matter of moving him toward a line — and the only person who can do that is somebody who can carry him, which is a siege problem, not a fight. On the floor he is slow and total: pick the ground and he is a wall that cannot be hurried off it.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him in any firm record, because the firm sells the jade and not the assessor, and an assessor who could be posted anywhere is not an assessor.

He holds the only copy of sixty seasons of floor notes and has never let them leave the isle, which is either professional caution or the single largest piece of leverage nobody has thought to take from him.

art.palette_notes: Firm indigo and bone white carry the figure, with one saturated accent in the jade chip at his throat and a second light source coming up out of the floor: the brine, drawn as pale reflected light on the underside of everything. So the picture is lit from above and below at once and the darkest values sit at his collar, which is the wettest part of him. Ink contours soft at the salt bloom and hard at the boots he has never removed.
