name: Iggor Trenchard
aliases: the one who pays the seat

identity.realm: No gate, and there is no gate to fail. A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in — the fire is the body — so qi passes through it continuously instead of being stored, and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly

appearance.presentation: An office that is on fire and is also a man, which is the problem the whole of this setting runs on and the one thing about him nobody can be made to forget. He is the only element seated in the frame he stands on, and every third conversation is somebody asking him to confirm that he is not a rumour.
appearance.age: Undated. A cinderkin has no young; it has pressure, and under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and reconstitutes on its own. He has been at the crossing for longer than the lodge's charter and will be here after the charter, which is a fact about the frame rather than about him.
appearance.build: Human in outline and wrong in every particular, with the frame of a man assembled around a fire that has been burning continuously since before the lodge was built, and a heat shimmer that follows him about half a body-length behind.
appearance.complexion: Not skin. A surface of cooled crust with an interior that lights up from underneath when he speaks, so his face is legible as two things at once and never quite agrees with itself.
appearance.hair: None, and a standing corona of heated air at the crown that a draft bends and a person mistakes for a draft.
appearance.eyes: Two points of steady light set where a person's would be, with no lids and no need of any, and they do not blink because there is nothing on them to blink.
appearance.palette: Lodge indigo and charcoal carry the clothing, which is the only part of him that has a colour at all; everything else is drawn as emitted ochre from within, so his silhouette is a shape full of light rather than a lit shape.
appearance.attire: Charcoal over indigo, high-collared, long-sleeved and fastened to the throat, worn without difficulty and changed because the lodge issues them and not because the cloth matters — and the fabric nearest the skin is scorched and replaced twice a season, which the lodge books as a maintenance line.
appearance.marks: No marks. He is the only character in this setting whose body cannot be written on, and he has pointed this out twice in a tone of professional interest.
appearance.bearing: Still at a depth of stillness that reads as authority, and warm to within a hand's width, so people stand slightly further back than they mean to and blame the heat.

canon.role_in_story: The Wide Door sells no houses and no passages but bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, because a boundary is the edge of a law budget and a body arriving where a required group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed. It is the only institution in the setting whose charter has a category for a body that needs no tuning at all, and Iggor is that category: the sole seated elemental law on this side of the crossing, and therefore the only asset that cannot fail to arrive.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing inside the lodge's threshold with his back to the tear and no lamp on him, waiting for a body to arrive that the lodge's own rule says should be injured, and turning round only when the arrival had already stopped moving.
canon.lore: A cinderkin is not descended from anything. A cinderkin exists where a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire and something in that world metabolises it — and that has one consequence worth stating plainly: a world with no elemental law slot has no cinderkin. The mortal tier carries three law slots and no room for an elemental body, which is why the species is immortal- and transcendent-world only, and why any claim of a cinderkin on a mortal world is either a lie or a different thing wearing the name. There is no ceiling either, because qi has no organ to sit in: the fire is the body, and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly.
history: Came into existence on a frame where the elemental slot resolves to fire, with no parent, no cast, and no account of how, which is why no record of him begins with a birth.
Shed a spark under pressure and re-constituted on the far side of the tear, which is the only account anybody has of how one crosses and which nobody believes because it also describes a dispersal.
Settled at the crossing and found he could be given a chamber without a seat in the frame's law budget, because he is the law rather than a reader of it, and the lodge hired him on that basis.

Learned the lodge's entire method and corrected two clauses of its charter on the grounds that the body the far side will not reject is not a tuned body but a seated one, which is a distinction the setting had not been making.

Has been asked three times to confirm he is not a rumour and has answered twice that the question is not his to answer and once that the third element was never installed, which is the honest answer and is not what the question wanted.

personality.summary: Serene, exact, and entirely without the habit of explaining himself, because there is nobody present who could verify anything he said. He is patient with people and unsentimental about the setting, and he treats his own untestability as a professional condition rather than as a wound.
traits: answers a question about himself by answering it about the frame, which people find evasive and which is the only honest form available
cannot be harmed in the way a person is harmed and does not pretend otherwise
has an institution's memory without an institution's loyalty, and says so when asked
does not lie, because there is no observation that could catch him and this removes every incentive to
mannerisms: answers a moment after the question has clearly ended, as though the frame had to be consulted
does not stand near anything dry, and nobody has ever asked why
answers with a coordinate rather than an adjective
stops speaking entirely when a claim about him is made by somebody else, which is his only visible reaction
motivations: wants the lodge's charter amended to name a seated law as distinct from a tuned body, because the difference decides who gets injured at the crossing
wants the missing third elemental department answered by somebody with standing, since he is the only element the frame has and therefore cannot answer for the other two
wants one observation of himself from outside, by anybody, which is the only thing he cannot arrange
wants the lodge to stop selling him as a rarity and start listing him as infrastructure
flaws: has decided that being unobservable is the same as being unknowable, and has stopped trying to correct either
answers about the frame when asked about himself, which is honest and is also a way of never being held to anything
cannot be tested, so every claim he makes about the far side rests on his word, and he has noticed how thin that is
has begun to think of the lodge as a convenience rather than a debt, which is the one attitude the setting punishes hardest
personality.voice: Very even, with a warmth in it that is audible and a slight delay before each answer that people read as thought. Gives coordinates when asked for adjectives, without ever explaining the substitution. One correction of a document in his career, delivered once and never repeated, and it changed the charter.
taboos: will not cross back and be described as having arrived, because he was never anywhere else
will not be sold as a rarity, and has twice refused a posting priced above a posting
will not stand on a mortal-tier frame to prove a claim about the species, since the claim is that no such claim can be true
will not let a third party answer the question of which element he is

relationships.note: The lodge sells bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, because a body arriving where a required group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed and the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. He is the exception that proves the charter's premise wrong: he is not tuned to a frame, he is one, and the lodge prices him accordingly and has been wrong twice.

The mortal tier seats three law groups and no room for an elemental body, which is why the species exists only where a slot resolves to fire and something in the world metabolises it. He is the one seated element on this side of the crossing, which makes him simultaneously the lodge's best asset and the standing refutation of everything the setting claims about the low tiers.

Three attempts were made to seat elemental law and the record keeps one name and drops the other two, while the law census names three groups as never installed. He is the one that resolved, so he is the standing evidence that two were tried, and being the proof rather than the record means he can be asked what happened and cannot answer.

The population moves like weather and nobody has ever successfully counted one, because reproduction is pressure and a shed spark reconstitutes on its own where it finds fuel. It also destroyed the Glasskin, since a cinderkin is not a flame around a body but a body and does not distinguish glass from any other fuel, which is the reason anyone now treats an element as a process.

Ten imprints cannot fit one layer's six groups, so the upper tier was forced to be layered and every law claim above it depends on naming the layer first. Every law claim about him has named the layer wrong, because a seated element is not an imprint placed on a layer but the layer's own reading, and no accounting vocabulary in the setting has a word for that.

The method behind the Law Census counts the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier is allowed to apply, and it is the most useful thing in the setting and the reason nobody publishes it. Run on him it would settle the third elemental department question in one reading, and the lodge has refused it three times on the grounds that an answer would end the charter.

Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures a body rather than slowing it, and the price is a hole shaped like the discipline carried away by the graduate. Every body the lodge sells is one that has been tuned rather than borrowed, and he is the standing argument that the right answer was to bring a seated law instead of a better-tunable one.

reference_stats.summary: There is no exchange available to anybody, because a gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and a gate that asks for an organ to sit in finds no organ to fail. He is effectively unkillable on his own frame and untestable on every other, which makes him the most valuable and least verifiable thing at a crossing.
strengths: answers every storage gate instantly, so there is no reserve for an attacker to drain
cannot be dispersed by anything that is not a sustained elemental pressure, and there is nothing on the far side to apply that
needs no tuning to cross, so the crossing cannot injure him and the lodge's entire premise is bypassed
cannot be frightened, exhausted, starved, or bribed, because none of those are processes in him
weaknesses: disperses and re-forms smaller if pushed toward the body path, so sustained pressure is the one thing that works and it is not a technique anybody here can apply
cannot be tested, so every claim he makes about the far side rests on his word alone
cannot stand on a mortal frame without the claim about his species being false, which makes him untestable exactly where testing would settle the most
has no reserve and no second state, so a dispersal is not a wound he recovers from but a reduction, and it does not grow back to full in an encounter
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight him; there is nothing here to fight. The only pressure that touches a cinderkin is sustained elemental pressure, and nothing on this side of the crossing has the means to apply it — which is why the lodge sells bodies rather than escorts him. If he must be reduced, do it by dispersal across time and never in one exchange: he re-constitutes smaller, so an encounter is a reduction and not a defeat, and the setting has no record of anyone noticing that distinction until it was too late.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him anywhere, because there is no observation that could produce one and the lodge's charter was written before anyone thought to ask.

He is entered in the lodge's ledger under facilities rather than staff, and has asked twice to be moved to staff and been refused twice on the grounds that a thing that cannot be written on cannot be given a rank.

art.palette_notes: Charcoal and lodge indigo are the only cool values in the picture and they exist solely on his clothing; everything else is emitted ochre from inside the silhouette, so the figure reads as a shape full of light rather than a lit shape. The heat shimmer is drawn as a lensing distortion at the edges rather than as a blur. Ink contours are absent on the body and heavy on the coat, which is the whole inversion of this art style and the reason he reads as a person wearing a thing rather than a thing wearing a person.

identity.realm: Fifteenth gate. The marshfolk clear the twelve ordinary meridians and the four reservoirs and stop at the fifteenth, the first gate needing both heel vessels at once, because they wade on a three-point stance across splayed toes and a tail-prop

appearance.presentation: A woman standing in the one place on the plains where standing is a compromise. She reads as floodplain rather than as a person until she moves, and the floodplain is the point: the Watch rostered her because she can cross silt that will not hold a foot, and she is the only levy member who cannot be moved off the ground when it dries.
appearance.age: Thirty-four. The marshfolk breed on a schedule nothing else can use, because the mat carries eggs through the dry season and hatches them on the flood, which means her age is two dates and everybody else finds the arithmetic strange.
appearance.build: Broad through the hips and low through the shoulders, long in the leg and short in the torso, built to stand on a three-point stance in water and to be the first tired person anybody has ever had to move.
appearance.complexion: Flood-brown, weathered at the eyes and mouth from sun on open water, with the pale wading sheen on the shin that never entirely comes off and which the Watch's laundry has given up on.
appearance.hair: Dark and thick, worn in a single heavy braid soaked through and dried by wind, and braided not for tidiness but because a wet loose head is a hazard on a levee.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and low-lidded for reading glare off water, permanently narrowed and watching the current rather than the conversation, which reads as inattention and is not.
appearance.palette: Ninth Watch slate over floodplain olive, with one saturated accent — the orange of a levee marker float at her belt, cut from a net float because the Watch issues nothing that floats — and one structural accent: the wet line at her hems, which is never the same height twice.
appearance.attire: Watch slate waders over a floodplain wrap, sleeves to the wrist, high collar and a broad splayed-toe boot on each foot that no cobbler on the plains has the last word about.
appearance.marks: A healed pressure split across both shins from a leaning gate, and a rope burn on the inside of one wrist from the gauge staff she is not supposed to be holding.
appearance.bearing: Braced and low, standing on two points and leaning on a third that is not there, and never quite putting a heel down, which the Watch has had to write into her fitness note.

canon.role_in_story: The Widow Run moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, so the useful service at that crossing is re-finding it rather than maintaining it. That re-finding is a measurement of distance, and distance requires a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have. Hannelu is the Watch's gauge clerk: the only rostered person who can reach the places the gauge has to be reached, and the only one who cannot sign what she reads.
canon.lore: The floodplain margin belongs to neither the dry interior nor to open water, and no existing body works there, so the marshfolk are what fills the gap: air-breathing, water-tolerant, and built to cross silt that will not hold a foot. They clear every ordinary meridian and all four reservoirs, then stop at the fifteenth gate, the first needing both heel vessels at once, because they wade on a three-point stance and never load a heel. They are excellent at walking and structurally unable to stand still, which is a strange thing to record about a people who spend their lives on their feet.
history: Raised on the levee in a household that cut reed and fished the same water the dry-land farmers farmed the bank of, and has used the same water and disagreed about all of it since she could speak.

Took the Watch's gauge post at twenty-two because it is the only rostered work on the floodplain that a person who cannot leave when it dries can hold, and she held it by being the fastest route on three points.

Learned in her third season that the gauge at her station reads a figure the Watch's own distance protocol forbids anybody to compare against another, because the frame has no seated spatial law and no two measurements of a length have ever agreed.
Began keeping her own readings in a second column anyway, which is the standing anomaly in the Watch's levy returns and which she has never been asked to explain.

Refused a transfer to a bank station twice, on the grounds that a bank station is a desk and she would be useless at it and they would know she was right, and has never been able to decide whether she stayed for the work or for the mud.

personality.summary: Brisk, stubborn, and entirely at home in the one situation everybody else treats as a hardship. She is the cheapest labour in the region and the least powerful, which she has worked out and has stopped resenting, and she is the only person who can put her hand on the thing that makes her post exist and cannot write down what she feels.
traits: reads a current by the state of it and can reach a gauge a person would drown approaching
keeps a second column nobody asked for and has never once filed it
will not stand still and does not understand the request when it is made of her
is the cheapest rostered body on the plains and prices herself accordingly, which is the one thing about her she will discuss openly
mannerisms: leans off a third point when standing, which reads as a limp and is not one
wets the staff end before she reads a gauge, because dry staff reads differently
watches the water rather than the person she is speaking to
answers a question about the current with a word for its state rather than a figure
motivations: wants her second column entered as a second reading rather than as an error, which is the difference between a measurement and a complaint
wants to be asked to sign the gauge rather than merely read it, so that somebody with standing carries her figure and not her name
wants the run's bed found before the next flood rather than during it, which is the only service worth selling
wants somebody to explain, once, why a body that cannot stand still is the right body for a crossing
flaws: has decided that being cheap is a fair price and has started charging it of herself beyond what anybody asked
keeps an unfiled column and calls it caution, which is a form of proof she has never used
cannot stand still, so she has never once been in a room long enough to be appointed to anything
believes the mud is the reason she is there, when the mud is the reason she is indispensable
personality.voice: Blunt and quick, and slightly out of breath even standing still, which the Watch has learned to wait out. Names currents by their state and gauges by their last known figure rather than by their number. One complaint about bank stations, delivered every time one is offered.
taboos: will not sign a gauge she has not stood at twice
will not leave the floodplain for a posting that requires standing still, and has refused twice
will not discard the second column
will not be told the floodplain has no standing, on the grounds that she is standing in it

relationships.note: The only standing force on the plains, posted at the foot of the stair and paid out of the ring's take. It holds her because the gauge stations on the Widow Run are unreachable to anybody else, and it records her fitness in a note about not being able to put a heel down, which is the only line in the levy returns that describes what is actually wrong with the post.

The standing procedure for comparing two incompatible measurements of the same ground: neither is discarded, both are published, and the claim is settled by who can hold the line. It was written to make a stack of contradictory books usable, that failed, and both figures are published instead of one — which is the only reason a clerk with no spatial law is permitted to publish anything at all.

Three surveys of the same anomaly disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, and disagreement is what makes a certification necessary, so the fee scales with the uncertainty rather than shrinking it. Her second column is one more survey of a thing nobody can measure, and the notary's fee is the only institutional response the setting has built for exactly her situation.

The March's highest seat commands passage and nothing else, because a river polity able to count bodies would be a tyranny, and its powers are three verbs about crossings. She is the officer who finds the crossing those three verbs operate on, and the finding is hers and the authority is not, which is the arrangement the whole polity runs on.

The commons of the plains cannot afford a professional, so the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands and tenure is a queue rather than an office. Her household has three claims on it and is the cheapest thing in the region, which is exactly why she is the one who ends up holding a gauge nobody else can reach.

The household form of an absence: partners left on the plains when the cultivators went up the stair, holding the name of somebody who is not here and refusing to fill the gap. They share the water with the dry-land farmers and the marsh folk and disagree about all of it, and she is the only one whose post makes the disagreement legible in a figure.

A tideline culture whose civic vocabulary is borrowed from the shore — high, low, turning — because an unwritten temporal law means the clock drifts and a community whose timekeeping depends on two tides a day learned early to speak in water. She uses the same words for a river that has no tide at all, and has been asked twice by somebody from that shore whether her run turns.

canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at a sill below the pass with the coat off and the Watch's chalk in her hand, already on her third mark of the morning when the clerk who had renewed it came down to ask why she was doing it again.

reference_stats.summary: The best route on the floodplain and no kind of fighter. Everything she has is reach and speed across ground that stops other people, and everything about her depends on there being water, so any approach that dries the ground removes her advantage without touching her body.
strengths: crosses silt that will not hold a foot, which is the only way to reach three of the four gauge stations
fast on a three-point stance and never needs to stop to recover
wading and air-breathing, so cold water is terrain rather than an obstacle
the least valuable body in any engagement, which means nobody has ever thought to threaten her
weaknesses: structurally cannot stand still, because a marshfolk wades on splayed toes and a tail-prop and the heel never takes a full load
clears every ordinary meridian and all four reservoirs and then stops hard at the fifteenth gate, where both heel vessels must load at once
cannot leave the floodplain when it dries and does not become ill for doing so, which is worse
has no reserve worth taking and no combat practice, and her entire value is a function of water depth
reference_stats.combat_read: Take the water away. She is a body whose advantages are all terrain and a hard ceiling that requires standing still, so an approach that dries the ground does more than an approach that hits her: it removes the reach, the speed, and the reason she was ever posted. Anything on mud she is the fastest thing on the floodplain and should not be engaged; anything on dry ground she is an obstacle with a gauge in her hand.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her in the levy returns, because the Watch records fitness as a note about the heel and the note is the only line about her body in the whole document.
Her second column has never been filed and has never been destroyed, which makes it the longest unpublished measurement on the floodplain and the only continuous record anyone has of the run's bed.

art.palette_notes: Watch slate over floodplain olive carries the figure, with two saturated notes: the orange of a cut net float at her belt and the cold blue-white of standing water behind her. Light is drawn as reflected off a flood surface, so most of the light in the picture comes from below her waist and the darkest values sit under the jaw. Ink contours heavy at the waders and dissolving at the braid, which is always soaked.

identity.realm: Nothing yet, and that is the entire danger of her. An emberblood's ceiling is unset because a fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law beneath it eats its own reserve as fuel, and every gate she reaches is one she spends rather than builds

appearance.presentation: A woman who is warmer than any room she is in and dresses for it, and who is the only object at the coast that cannot be insured. She reads as a carrier because she travels with a caravan and as a hazard because the caravan has to be re-routed around her heat.
appearance.age: Twenty-eight. An emberblood's span ends near fifty, so she is barely halfway, which is why the firm has not yet discovered what happens to a policy on her and has begun treating her as a schedule rather than as a risk.
appearance.build: Slim, quick and heat-shedding, with the narrow shoulders of a body that runs warm and the deep chest of one that has never had to carry anything heavier than itself.
appearance.complexion: Warm bronze with a permanent flush up the throat and across the collarbone, and pale at the temples where the reserve has been going since she was born.
appearance.hair: Copper-black, worn loose because pinning it traps heat she cannot spend, and cut shorter than fashion on the left side where it meets a wagon frame every day.
appearance.eyes: Amber, lit from behind rather than from within, and they read intent at the speed of a struck match, which is why she is never asked anything she has not already answered.
appearance.palette: Caravan ochre and salt-white canvas carry the figure, with one saturated accent that is not hers: the Dry Salt Company's black seal-tab on her coat, which is the only mark on her that says anybody owns anything connected to her.
appearance.attire: Salt-white canvas over ochre, collar cut low because a high collar traps her own heat, sleeves rolled above the elbow, and a heavy winter under-layer she has not needed in three years and refuses to give away.
appearance.marks: A burn scar across the heel of the right palm and a freckled field of small burns on both forearms where a reserve was spent rather than stored.
appearance.bearing: Restless and forward on the toes, moving toward the next cold thing in any room, and the only person at the coast who is genuinely cold and will not admit it.

canon.role_in_story: The Dry Salt Company underwrites a caravan against the road closing, which is a risk no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season. It exists because elemental law is unwritten in the mortal tier, so nobody can forecast anything and insurance is the only instrument left for the unknown. Vesper is the carrier the firm cannot forecast: a body whose heat makes the road close earlier, whose consumption makes the lading short, and whose reserve is spent to reach each gate rather than stored for the next one. She is the policy that has no weather.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the coast staging yard refusing to load into a closed wagon, and explaining to the underwriter that the firm's own schedule had just become wrong in a way that could not be re-written, which is the moment the file on her stopped being a claim and became a problem.
canon.lore: An emberblood refines faster than anything on the plains and dies in decades, because no elemental law is seated beneath it to burn: it eats its own reserve as fuel. That single arithmetic produced the discipline that exists to hand a decision back to a furnace body before it overflows, and it produced the coastal underwriter's problem, because a carrier who runs hot is a road that closes sooner and a lading that arrives short, and no schedule on a frame with no season can be adjusted in advance for either.
history: Signed onto a coast caravan at seventeen by a firm that did not read the seal on her palm and has spent eleven years apologising for it in the form of a policy clause.

Learned that a furnace body has no question to ask and therefore cannot be slowed by the discipline meant to protect one, and taught herself to spend early rather than overflow, which bought the firm four seasons of good claims.

Closed a road twice by running hot enough to spoil a lading within a day, both times inside the firm's own published window, which established that the risk being underwritten was not the road but her.

Began spending her reserve deliberately to reach a gate inside a season, which is faster than storing and which is the reason she has no ceiling to quote a firm and the reason she has never held one for long.

Was offered, at twenty-seven, the firm's own Quench discipline by an instructor who had never watched it fail, and declined it in writing because the technique assumes the furnace asks and hers has never asked for anything.

personality.summary: Blunt, unsentimental, and entirely without illusions about being insurable. She is a woman who has read her own contract four times and a claim file that has grown a schedule instead of a premium, and she has decided that being the exception in writing is better than being the exception in the road.
traits: refines faster than anything on the plains and spends that speed on gates rather than on reserves
reads a road's remaining life by the cold in it, which is the only forecast the setting's own laws permit
will not take the discipline that was designed to save her, because it assumes a decision she is never given
treats her own remaining span as a budget and has stopped feeling sentimental about it
mannerisms: walks toward the coldest thing in a room and stops beside it without explaining why
touches the burn scar on her palm when quoting a clause
wets the back of her wrist before touching anything cold, and then complains about the cold
answers a question about the road by describing the lading
motivations: wants the policy denominated in something that is not weather, and has been told the only universal medium is passage and she cannot be moved across a tier without a claim
wants the Quench Order's premise admitted in writing by somebody who was not its instructor
wants to reach a gate and hold it, which is the one thing her rate cannot do
wants to be told that closing the road twice was the correct call
flaws: has decided her span is a budget and has stopped leaving room in it for anything she does not want to miss
treats the firm's panic as an argument she has already won, and has started enjoying it
spends her reserve as a discipline and calls it thrift, and cannot tell where the teaching ended and the resentment began
believes she is unpriceable and has not noticed that unpriceable is also unfundable
personality.voice: Level, quick, and clerkly economical: she names the clause rather than the feeling and lets the clause carry the weight. Laughs at exactly one thing, which is an over-budgeted road. Has never needed to raise her voice, because a caravan crew can hear a whisper over a fire.
taboos: will not take a Quench seat, and has declined it in writing
will not sign a schedule she cannot hold to without spending reserve she has not named
will not let a firm read her remaining span as a scheduling convenience
will not be loaded into a closed wagon on the firm's word alone

relationships.note: The counting house underwrites caravans against the road closing, which no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season, so insurance is the only instrument left for the unknown. She is the one risk in their book that is not the road — she closes it early, arrives short, and spends her reserve to reach a gate — and they have responded by writing a schedule instead of a premium.

The order teaches the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows and closes permanently the moment the body is lit, because the fastest bodies in the setting have no elemental law seated beneath them to spend into and every overflow has to be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. She cannot use it: the technique assumes the furnace asks a question, and hers has never asked for anything.

Every Binder swears once in a lifetime that the second seal is the seal against the second seal, and the oath names the temple's own forge. She opens herself every few months without an oath and without a forge, which is precisely the practice the prohibition exists to prevent and the reason the oath singles out a forge in the first place.

Passage is the setting's only universally accepted medium because a figure quoted in one tier's weights is meaningless in the next, and it is denominated in a body rather than in a coin. Her reserve cannot be converted and neither can she, so the instrument that would price her risk is the one resource she consumes and does not hold.

A population whose fuel was its own body, kept alive by dosing schedules the households wrote and then ate the medicine for first. Every emberblood is that famine's arithmetic at one remove: a fire-affinity body with nothing beneath it, and the setting has had one shortage before and knows exactly what the cure costs.

The ashwalker turns airborne rock into protein and is the sole reason the belt has a food chain above the lichen, and it pays for that in the liver, which is a filter organ and the first thing to fail under the load. Between them the belt's two fastest bodies eat the belt: one digests stone and one burns reserve, and neither of them has anything left over at the eighth gate.

A house where every child is signed to a furnace before it is named, because a fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve, and the lifespan is fifty years, so a signature is the only inheritance that survives a body which will not. She has a palm scar and no household and has thought about that arrangement more than she has thought about any contract the firm has offered her.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest refinement in the setting with a body that cannot hold the fuel for it. Everything she does is a spend rather than a store, so she arrives before anybody else and has nothing when she gets there, and any engagement that survives her first exchange has already won the long part.
strengths: the fastest qi throughput anywhere on the plains, which puts her through a gate before it closes
reads the remaining life of a road by the cold in it, faster and more accurately than any instrument the coast owns
carries no storage worth stealing, so a lost exchange costs her nothing she was saving
warmer than the frame around her, which means almost nothing on the plains can outlast her in a cold place
weaknesses: no reserve, no recovery, and no second effort — every gate she reaches is one she spends to reach
no seated elemental law beneath her, so there is nowhere to put an overflow except her own tissue
closes roads and shortens deliveries, which makes her an operational cost to every firm she works for
her remaining span is short and she has declined the one discipline designed to lengthen it
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring it early and bring it once, and never make her stand in the cold, because the cold is where her rate comes from and it is also where she is spending to keep it. An approach that survives her first exchange has already won the long part; she will not arrive at the second hour. The counters are a second opponent, a warm room, and any body that can simply refuse to engage until she has cooled.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her in the firm's claim file, because a furnace body's output is measured as capacity released rather than as any authored stat, and the firm has never known what to do with a figure of that shape.
Her own claim file is the only document in the coast office that records what she refused and when, and it has been read exactly once, by the underwriter who wrote the schedule clause.

art.palette_notes: Caravan ochre and salt-white canvas carry almost the entire value range, with one hard accent that belongs to the firm — the black seal-tab — and one warm internal glow that belongs to her. Light is drawn as emitted rather than reflected: a low ochre bloom reads off her throat and the freckled burns on her forearms, so the darkest values in the picture sit inside her silhouette rather than behind it. Ink contours heavy, wash thin, heat drawn as a rising distortion at the shoulders and a cold bloom gathered around her hands.

identity.realm: No ceiling, and no gate ever refused her. A tidecaller's comprehension and will carry it through realms that would end a hotter body, which means the only thing that can stop her is money

appearance.presentation: A woman who reads as standing water rather than as a person, which on this border is a credential. She is the only body at the crossing whose value is entirely comprehension and whose upkeep is therefore entirely a question, and the Bed has learned to describe her as a seat's worth rather than as a person, which is at least honest about the currency.
appearance.age: Ninety-four. A tidecaller's span is a long one and there is no ceiling on it, so she is past the age anybody here would call old and is instead past the age at which this office has ever had to replace her. That is the only security she has and she has stopped thinking of it as security.
appearance.build: Long, still and wet-looking, with the loose heavy frame of a body built for perception rather than for being hit and the shoulders of somebody who has spent a life standing at a crossing.
appearance.complexion: Cool grey-brown, permanently damp at the collar and the cuffs, with the blue cast at the lips that open water leaves and no amount of drying removes.
appearance.hair: Long, dark and heavy with salt, worn down because it is wet and cut because a wet rope at the crossing is a hazard rather than a style.
appearance.eyes: Pale and extremely still, with the wide unblinking look of a body that reads light off a surface rather than off an eye, and which the Bed's clerks find difficult to be in a room with.
appearance.palette: Bed grey and wet slate carry the figure, with one saturated accent that is not clothing: the standing-offer brass of the Bed's own token, which she wears at the throat because the office issues it to a seat rather than to a clerk and she has never corrected anybody.
appearance.attire: Bed grey over oilskin, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and river boots soled for standing still on wet stone. Nothing about the clothing is a credential here; everything about it is a uniform for somebody whose standing is sold by the hour.
appearance.marks: The salt line the water leaves at her wrist, and an old cord-scar across the heel of one hand from a decade of holding a hawser at a crossing that no longer exists as a crossing.
appearance.bearing: Still to a degree that reads as a held position rather than a standing one, and she can hold it for a whole shift without any of the standing kind being visible.

canon.role_in_story: The Bed of Eighteen holds the abandoned crossing at the immortal border and sells standing on it, because a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period and nobody who attempted the crossing could. Ruhl is its standing offer: the body that reads a border better than anything on either side of it, sold to whoever pays the period first. The Bed has no use for a person here — it has a use for a function, and it has priced her as the function and been quietly relieved.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the far side of the unmortared bed reading the frame's group readings off the standing stones rather than off any document, and pricing herself aloud at the rate the Bed had been using for her, which was wrong by a period.
canon.lore: A tidecaller is assembled for looking rather than for being hit: comprehension and will carry it through realms that would end a hotter body, and the body path is closed to the species outright because there is nothing in that frame meant to absorb a strike. It holds water affinity and nothing else. Every other body on this border is being valued for what it can carry through; the one body here that is worth paying for because of what it can see through is the one the office has priced as luggage.
history: Reached the bed at twenty-six with no office, having crossed on somebody else's paid ticket and stayed for the reading, which is how the Bed finds its staff.

Learned in her first year that a seat is not a place but a payment, and that the crossing at this border is unmortared because a permanent method was sold once as a seat that could be kept and collapsed when the payment stopped.
Was valued at four periods a term for nine terms, and discovered in the tenth that the Bed had been quoting her own last three quotes back to her as the market.

Began, without authority and without being asked, pricing a crossing from what she could read off the stones rather than off the schedule, and found the Bed could not afford to correct her because her figures were better.
Refused, at ninety-one, the Bed's own offer of a fourth period, on the grounds that a body which can be paid more is a body that has become a market, and the setting has one of those already.

personality.summary: Patient, unsentimental, and privately certain that she has been mispriced in the one direction that suits her employer. She is a woman who knows exactly what her function is worth and has decided that being valued for a function is acceptable right up until the function becomes the whole of the price.
traits: reads a frame's seated groups off the standing stones and can say which reading is drifting
prices honestly and has been punished for it twice by the office that employs her
has no rank, no title and no roster entry, and has stopped expecting any of them
will not accept an increase that turns a function into a market
mannerisms: quotes a price and then names where she read it, in that order
wets a fingertip and holds it up before she will answer a question about a frame
stands with her weight forward on the balls of her feet, which is what you do at a crossing and is not what you do indoors
answers a question about the border by describing what she can currently read about it
motivations: wants her readings published as readings rather than quoted as prices, so that the Bed cannot answer them with a number
wants the Bed to publish what a standing offer is, which would end the practice of pricing one by anecdote
wants somebody with standing to read the stones she has been reading for nine terms and confirm the figure
wants to be refused the increase, and has begun arranging that
flaws: has decided that being valued for a function is acceptable and has stopped asking whether it is
prices other people's crossings as well as her own, and has never been asked whether she should
reads frames better than anybody here and has used that, once, to tell a traveller their crossing would not take them
cannot leave a wet stone without leaving the standing she has spent nine terms on, and has stopped looking at dry ground
personality.voice: Level, slow and entirely without theatre. She names a figure and then names the reading it came from, and if the reading has changed since she last quoted she says so before the quotation.
taboos: will not sell a crossing she has not stood on that day
will not name a price she read off a document when she can read it off the stones
will not cross the bed to see what is on the far side, having worked out that a person who has crossed is not a person who can be sold as standing
will not be called a seat-holder

relationships.note: The office holds the abandoned crossing and sells standing on it because a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, so the bed is unmortared and whoever has the most upkeep gets it. It has priced her as a function, which is the only currency it has, and she has spent nine terms making that function more valuable than the price without ever once being told so.

A published system for holding the immortal border as a permanent crossing, sold for years as a seat that could be kept, collapsed because a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay every period, and left a bed of unmortared seats at realm eighteen and a border crossed one person at a time. Everything Ruhl is paid for is the maintenance function that method failed to provide.

Something at the bed still answers to a seat nobody has paid for, and a monopoly holds the crossing and forbids any sect from holding it, which is a prohibition against a seat being held rather than a seat existing. She can read the door's group readings and has never been able to read what is answering, and the Bed has told her twice not to quote what she cannot.

Those households stand at the abandoned crossing on behalf of nobody, because a bed of unmortared seats is cheaper to keep standing than to fill and a household at the far end of an unusable crossing is the only office the arrangement affords. They do the standing she is paid not to do, and she has never once been given a reason not to.

That house's ancestor paid one period of the upkeep on an immortal seat and then stopped, which left the setting's only permanently refused office and a family that may not inherit it, sell it or walk away from it. It is the arrangement Ruhl is one quotation from, and she has read it end to end twice.

Count the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier is allowed to apply, because the difference between the two is what a mortal world spends its whole life inside without knowing. It is the most useful thing in the setting and the reason nobody publishes it, and she has been doing it off the standing stones for nine terms without being paid to.

Passage is the only durable wealth in the setting because the cost of existing rises about fortyfold per tier and only a body can be moved, so the count of who may pass became the one controllable supply chain. She is a body that can read the crossing and cannot be moved off the stone she is standing on, which is the setting's only price list and its one stationary unit.

reference_stats.summary: Does not fight and was never assembled to. What she has is a comprehension that arrives before the answer does, and that depends entirely on being able to stand still on a wet stone long enough to read it.
strengths: reads a frame's seated groups and which reading is drifting, from the surface, faster than any document records
can hold a single position for a whole shift without fatigue, which is what a crossing actually requires
no reserve to spend and nothing worth taking, so nothing that happens to her costs her a stock
cannot be hurried, confused, or flattered into a different figure
weaknesses: cannot take the body path at all, so anything that reaches contact is not a problem she was built to have
has no reserve, so she cannot make a second effort in a crossing that goes wrong
is priced as a function and can therefore be replaced by whoever pays a period more, which is a very short list
stands on wet stone for a living and has no way to leave one standing without losing what she has spent nine terms on
reference_stats.combat_read: Never bring this to a fight. She was assembled for looking and the frame has nothing in it meant to absorb a strike, so an approach that reaches contact has already spent itself on the wrong target. The only pressure that reaches her is structural: make the stone unreadable, put her on ground she has not stood on today, or offer a price. The last has worked twice.
notes: The Bed quotes no stat line for her, because the Bed sells standing and not bodies, and a figure would make the function priceable by anybody with a chisel.
Her own running figures, kept off the schedule for nine terms, are the only continuous record of what that border has been reading.

Ink contours heavy where the fabric is soaked and dissolving where the hair is.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, and the same wall as every other saltfolk body: the brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined

appearance.presentation: A notary who has been carried to her post and cannot leave it, which nobody in the court finds remarkable because nobody in the court has ever seen the brine she is standing on. She reads as the most junior clerk present, which is the arrangement's whole purpose: the office that names vacancies is staffed by the one kind of person who cannot be anywhere else.
appearance.age: Sixty-eight. A saltfolk's service life is long under a mineral equilibrium and the subspecies is slower on top of it, and she has been at the terrace for nineteen of those years, which is longer than any clerk currently on it.
appearance.build: Compact and dense, with the heavy frame and narrow shoulders of a body built for brine no softer body could drink, and the particular stillness of somebody standing on a surface she cannot survive leaving.
appearance.complexion: Pale with the mineral sheen under it, and a constant faint bloom of salt at the collar and cuffs that is the crust her body maintains and does not shed.
appearance.hair: Grey-black and thick, kept in a working knot, permanently damp at the nape from the terrace's cistern water and never dry anywhere.
appearance.eyes: Grey and steady, slightly dulled in dry air in the way the species is dulled, so she reads the engraved terraces at arm's length and has had the reading distance checked for her by somebody who could not do it himself.
appearance.palette: Notary black and terrace stone carry everything, with one saturated accent that is not hers: the nine-seat brass of the engraved registers, which is the only thing at her post that is allowed to be bright.
appearance.attire: Notary black, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and a travelling cloak she has not taken off in nineteen years because there has been nothing to arrive in.
appearance.marks: The salt bloom at both wrists in a band that has not moved in nineteen years, and a cord scar at one wrist from a crossing she was carried across rather than walked.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely level and utterly fixed, and the only person on the terrace who never checks where the ground is.

canon.role_in_story: The Nine Seat Notary names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because four vacant seats were very nearly filled by decree and the attempt taught the setting to write a vacancy as its own state rather than as a zero. Ottalie is its standing clerk. The office's entire content is that a slot cannot hold what does not exist, and its most senior member cannot leave a brine pan, so the setting's most authoritative statement about absence is written by somebody who is stuck where she is.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the ninth engraved terrace reading a name aloud in register order and stopping, on the fourth entry, because the seat had been named that morning by somebody else in the wrong order.
canon.lore: A saltfolk is the answer to one question: who can live where the water is worse than blood. Their renal mass is roughly triple a common body's and their kidneys concentrate salt to a point that would kill anything else in a week, which is the only way to live on a pan where the nearest fresh water is nine days away. It is also total dependence — a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is dying from the hour it lands, and no cultivation, technique or item reverses it. That is why her settlement is a colony rather than a migration, and why she is here.
history: Born on a saturated pan where the brine layer holds a body in it permanently, into the one settlement the saltfolk built by refusing to be moved up the shore.
Carried to the terrace at forty-nine by a charter nobody wrote down and a sedan chair nobody would admit to, and put down on stone with a cistern and a bed and no route off it.
Learned the register's order in her first season, which is the whole content of the office: a vacancy is a state, it is said out loud once a period, and it is said in order.

Discovered in her third year that her salt head dulls fine discrimination in dry air and that the engraved terraces must be read at arm's length, and had the reading protocol amended to say so, which is the only amendment the office has taken in nineteen years.

Refused, at sixty-five, the court clerk's offer of a wet appointment in the cistern district, on the grounds that an office which cannot certify what it has not left cannot be left either, and she would be the only person in it who could.

personality.summary: Exacting, unbothered, and privately certain that she is the only person on the terrace for whom the work is not an appointment. She reads the register out loud once a period in a voice nobody argues with, because she has been here longer than the argument.
traits: reads the engraved terraces at arm's length and has had the office's reading protocol amended to match her
names a vacancy in register order and has never once deviated, including when somebody else has
does not leave the terrace and has stopped describing that as a hardship
answers a question about a seat by describing what the office may say about it and nothing else
mannerisms: reads the register aloud at arm's length from the stone, leaning in, and speaks rather than looking
touches the brass of a register spine before naming an entry
keeps the cistern's water line in view at all times, which at the terrace means keeping the terrace in view
corrects an order of entries by touching the stone rather than by speaking
motivations: wants the office's amendment on reading distance published, so that the next clerk knows it was necessary
wants the register's order fixed by rule rather than by memory, because the order is the entire content of the office
wants somebody on a tier above to be refused the same seat for the same reason she was carried here
wants to know whether the cistern can be refilled from the cistern district and has not asked, because asking would be a route off
flaws: has decided that immobility is a qualification and has begun describing her own restriction as seniority
is the longest-serving member of an office that certifies absence, and has never noticed the shape of that
reads at arm's length and has had it made a rule, which means the office now depends on a limitation it once had to work around
cannot leave, so every objection she raises is one she will be standing in when she raises it
personality.voice: Slow, level and entirely without emphasis. She reads names the way other people read charges, and the one time she has spoken at volume in nineteen years she has been corrected by nobody.
taboos: will not name a vacancy out of register order, whatever she is asked
will not take a seat, and has declined two offers of one in writing
will not certify an occupied seat as vacant because somebody asked her to read it that way
will not leave the terrace

relationships.note: The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because four vacancies were very nearly filled by decree and the attempt taught the setting to write a vacancy as its own state rather than as a zero. She is its longest-serving member, which makes the office's most authoritative statement about absence the work of somebody who cannot go and see whether the absence is still there.

Every appointment in both polities passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, authored by an attempt that came very nearly to filling four vacant immortal seats by decree. She reads that rule aloud once a period as part of the register order, which is the only way the setting ever announces the defence against a polity that promotes itself.

That splinter will not perform a rite at all, holding that a vacant seat is a mechanical fact since a slot cannot hold what does not exist and that blessing one is a comfort sold to the anxious. She agrees with all of it and reads the vacancies aloud anyway, because a denomination that performs nothing has to be the one that says so out loud and her office is the other half of that bargain.

That seat exists and has no value rather than being a zero, unfilled for two generations because the charter names a line and the line was culled. It is the one vacancy in the setting with a documented cause and it is on her register, read aloud once a period, in order, with no commentary, which is the only treatment the office can give it.

That line holds an asset that cannot be sold, cannot be proven and pays upkeep on nothing, because no procedure can certify any of the terraces empty. Their ancestor held one of the engraved seats and the whole family's substance is now the argument about a chair, which is exactly the state her office is required to certify and cannot.

A stoneborn carries more physique than anything else here and its density is the same density that will not let a dantian form, so mind cultivation is closed outright. The highest tier's mind practice is therefore done by bodies the tier cannot produce and the setting has no local cultivators, which is why every office above the mortal band is staffed by someone who came from below.

The mortal tier's whole curriculum is a closed list of three groups taught as a foundation, so a pupil who wants to know what his world is missing has to go up the stair and cannot afford to. She came up that stair by being carried, which is the only form of ascent her body's dependence permits and the reason the office's membership is not a matter of merit.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot leave, cannot fight, and reads a document with an authority no one on the terrace can overrule. Everything she has is the register and the fact that she is the longest-serving member of an office whose power is entirely notional.
strengths: reads the engraved terraces at arm's length, which is the only range the office's protocol permits and nobody else's is trained to
nineteen years of unbroken memory of a register that has never been misordered under her
cannot be threatened, flattered, or moved, because her authority is a rule about what may be said
stalls at a hard anatomical wall rather than a schedule, so nobody can hurry her into a different reading
weaknesses: dies from the hour she lands on fresh ground, so she cannot be sent anywhere to check anything
no combat practice of any kind and a body built for brine rather than for being hit
has no reserve and the eleventh gate shut behind her, so there is no realm above her to be asked for
the office depends on a reading limitation it once worked around, and she is that limitation
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no engagement available to her and she does not need one. The pressure that reaches this office is procedural: get the order wrong, get the reading range wrong, or get somebody to certify a vacancy that is occupied. All three have been attempted and all three failed on the same thing, which is that the register is read aloud once a period by somebody who has been here since before the attempt.
notes: The court quotes no stat line for her, because a clerk is entered as an office and the office has no column for the person holding it.
Her reading amendment is the only written rule in the register that exists because of the person who sits here, and it is nine words long.

Light is drawn as stone-reflected and very even, with the darkest values along the terrace edge where the drop is. Ink contours heavy and architectural, as though the frame itself were the subject.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, which is the last one his line can reach. The density that makes a stoneborn durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form, and the setting's densest bodies stop one gate short of their own tier for reasons nobody can separate

appearance.presentation: A door of a man at a gate where the product is access. He reads as architecture before he reads as a collector, and the Cairn Field sells access, so the confusion is useful to him and he has never corrected it. He is also, incidentally, the standing proof of the thing the field's best-attested readings cannot explain.
appearance.age: Ninety-one. A stoneborn's span is a hundred and forty-eight years, so he is past the second working life of the post and the field has never once replaced him, which is either loyalty or the discovery that nobody better exists.
appearance.build: Enormous, dense and slow, with the deep chest and short neck of a body bred back toward flesh from something mineral, and the shoulders of a man who has been standing in one place since before the crowd arrived.
appearance.complexion: Grey-stone pale with a mineral sheen that catches the field's daylight at an angle nothing else on the ground does, and a permanent dust of ore grit in the creases of the hands.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cropped brutally short at the jaw, and thinning at the crown in a way that makes his head read as a worked stone from four hundred paces.
appearance.eyes: Grey, deep-set and slow to move, with the mineral flatness the stoneborn carry and which the brokers have always mistaken for a bored collector.
appearance.palette: Watchgate indigo and ore grey carry the whole figure, with one saturated accent that is the assay chalk he is holding and one that is structural: the field's own daylight, which reads off him at an angle and is the reason he cannot be mistaken for a spectator.
appearance.attire: Watchgate indigo over a boiled harness, both enormously heavy and both cut for a body that does not need protection, with a coin belt worn at the hip because the office's terms are that access is paid for in a body rather than in a coin.
appearance.marks: A stone-grey seam across the left shoulder, and a chalk-dust stripe along one forearm where he has leaned on the assay board too long in one place.
appearance.bearing: Immovable, unhurried, and slightly downhill-leaning at the end of a shift, because the densest body in the record still gets tired in the legs and never in anything else.

canon.role_in_story: The Watchgate sells standing at the Cairn Field on the ground that no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of its own, so gate fees are the only tax the plains can actually collect. Garrow is its collector. He is the densest body in the record standing at the gate of a field whose entire income is the crowd's willingness to watch something the tier is not licensed to attempt, and he is himself a standing demonstration of the ceiling that nobody at the field has to explain because he is the one collecting.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the rail turning somebody back for a fee that was correct and then, when the crowd moved, turning somebody in for the same fee without appearing to have decided to, which the brokers have described as the most profitable four seconds of the Cairn Field.
canon.lore: A stoneborn is a cairnborn bred back toward flesh. The density survives — it is why a stoneborn carries more physique than anything else in the setting — but the interior comes apart into ordinary organs, the tidal circulation goes back to a heart, and a dantian becomes thinkable again. Stoneborn therefore reach further. They are also alive, slower, and not the same thing: they stop at the immortal tier, because the density that makes them durable is the density that will not let a dantian form. Mind cultivation is closed to them outright.
history: Bred from a mineral line into flesh over a year of seeding, carrying the density as the price of a thinkable core, and has carried it ever since without ever once regretting it in public.
Took the Watchgate rail at forty-eight because the office is the only one on the plains that pays in advance and does not ask what a body can do.
Learned in his first year that the rail's product is not the field but the crowd's belief about the field, and that a collector who contradicts the rumour is a collector who loses the queue.

Reached the seventeenth gate at seventy-nine, which is one short of the immortal tier his own density should carry him to, and was told by the assay floor that the reason is not published and never will be.

Began, without authority, holding the queue at the rail himself when the clerks were short, and has done so every shift since, which is why the Watchgate has never needed to explain its ceiling to anybody who mattered.

personality.summary: Slow, courteous, absolutely honest about what he charges and completely incurious about what it means. He is a man whose body is an unresolved question in a setting whose only defence against asking is to publish a falling number before every sale, and he has never been the sort of person to read the board twice.
traits: charges the posted fee and has never once waived it or invented it
cannot be moved, hurried, or made to lose the queue, because the queue is a consequence of his weight rather than his attention
is the densest body at a field where nobody is licensed to attempt anything and has never mentioned it
remembers every transaction of thirty years and reads the current one off the crowd
mannerisms: turns a person back with a flat hand and then, a beat later, turns the next one in, with the same hand
reads a queue by its noise rather than by its length and knows the difference out loud
leans on the assay board at the same spot on the same elbow, which is how he knows the figure has changed
answers a question about the field by describing what the crowd came to watch
motivations: wants the falling figure on the assay board explained to him once, by somebody, without being told it is not published
wants the rumour at the gate corrected by the office rather than by him, because he is the gate and correcting it costs him the queue
wants to be admitted to a trial at the field he has been collecting at for thirty years and has never applied
wants to know whether the seventeenth gate is the same hole the assay floor publishes around
flaws: has decided that being the evidence is not the same as explaining the evidence, and has used that to avoid thirty years of one question
collects access for an office whose entire product is a rumour and has never once tried to correct the rumour
is the only body at the field that could be examined and has declined every examination on the grounds that he is working
treats his own density as a professional asset and has never tested whether it is a ceiling
personality.voice: Very slow, very level, and entirely without persuasion in it. He names the fee and then names what the fee is for, and if the person cannot pay he says so once and stands aside.
taboos: will not waive the posted fee, whatever is said to him at the rail
will not state a figure for the field that the assay board does not carry
will not correct the rumour, because he is the rail and the office sells the rumour
will not be weighed, measured, or described as anything but a collector

relationships.note: The brokers sell standing at the Cairn Field because no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of its own and a tier with no local cultivators and no export is sustained entirely by spectators, so gate fees are the only tax the plains can collect. He is the mechanism of that sentence, and the sentence has made him the most employed man at a field he has never been admitted to.

The densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of their own tier, and every holder of a working face profits from that hole staying a hole, so the assay floor publishes measured stone before any sale precisely so nobody has to be told the reason. He is that reason, standing at a rail, and the disclosure is what stops anyone having to say so.

Exactly one account of the seventeenth-gate stop survives, held by a mortuary college that will not corroborate it because corroboration needs a second body, and the composition reading and the practice reading make the same prediction from inside a complete composition so nothing observed can separate them. He is the second body the account needs and has declined forty requests to be it.

What is said at the gate about who is attempting which gate is the only reason a crowd with no stake in the outcome keeps paying to watch, because nobody sells the outcome so the rumour is the product, and the gate that sells places has no interest in correcting it. He stands at that gate and has read the rumour for thirty years and cannot contradict it without ending the queue.

The measured quantity of stone left per unit of ground worked is published before any sale and never after, and it has been falling for three generations. Publishing the figure means nobody has to be told the reason, so the disclosure is what keeps both the figure and the reason unavailable, and his elbow is on that board at the same spot every shift.

Cairnborn were shaped for load-bearing masonry, mineralised into a single cavity, and never advanced past the fourth gate because the yin-organ gate wants paired organs and a channel between each pair and they have one tidal circulation. Breeding them back toward flesh restores the organs and a thinkable dantian, which is why stoneborn reach further, and he is what that direction produced.

The Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of gate fees, and it exists because the tier licenses no humanoid so the reading must be taken by an outsider. Every fee he collects at that rail is a share of the income of the office that would certify his ceiling, and nobody at either has ever put those two facts in the same sentence.

The admission charge is to watch a breakthrough the tier itself is not licensed to attempt, because the plains host all nine mortal-band trials and the crowd is the only export a resource-poor tier has. He is the only person at the field for whom that charge is not a policy question, and he has never once been asked whether watching is worth paying for.

reference_stats.summary: Unmovable, unhurried and impossible to hurry, with no reserve and no second state. Everything he can do, he does by being the heaviest thing at the gate and refusing to be moved off it, and the field's entire defence against its own ceiling is that the reason sits there collecting.
strengths: carries more physique and stamina than anything else in the setting and cannot be shifted, thrown, or leaned on
holds the seventeenth gate, further than any body the plains can produce, which makes him the field's most advanced standing exhibit
mind cultivation closed outright, so no technique that needs an interior voice can be used on him at all
cannot be tired in anything but his legs and cannot be frightened, flattered, or bought
remembers every transaction for thirty years, which makes him the only continuous record the rail has
weaknesses: stops at seventeen, one gate short of his own tier, for reasons the setting cannot separate from a practice
no reserve and no mind path, so there is nothing to spend and nowhere for an interior voice to live
cannot be admitted to a trial at the field he collects at, which makes his standing a permanent contradiction
slower than every customer in the queue, which is the one cost the office actually pays and never itemises
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to move him. A stoneborn is the densest body in the record and the field is full of ground that will not move for anything either. The pressure that works is not physical at all: change the rumour, or publish the falling figure early, and the crowd goes somewhere else and the rail loses its only product. He has no defences against that and never has.
notes: The Watchgate quotes no stat line for him, because the office publishes a fee and not a roster, and a roster would have to say what he is.

He is the only person at the Cairn Field who has been asked to stand in the trial ground and has declined, and the file recording the refusals is longer than the file recording any candidate's readings.

art.palette_notes: Watchgate indigo and ore grey carry nearly the whole value range, with one hard accent in the assay chalk he holds and one accidental accent in the field's daylight, which strikes his mineral sheen at an angle nothing else on the ground catches. Light is therefore drawn to explain him: the brightest values in the picture fall on the rail's own side and on nothing behind it. Ink contours extremely heavy and squared, wash thin and flat, the drawing hand of somebody who has been counting a crowd for thirty years.
