identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, held on the flank vessels and lost again every winter. A longwinter's flank pair needs two warm gradients held at once and the species has one, briefly, in summer

appearance.presentation: A sworn member of a house whose unbounded office recognises no stat at all, which she reads as freedom and which is in fact a description. She reads as a body's own warmth in a cold room — she is always slightly the warmest thing in any space — and the Vine's sworn are all slightly warm things in cold rooms, which is how she is spotted.
appearance.age: A hundred and eleven. A longwinter's span is a hundred and sixty years and she has used thirty of them being useful and none of them staying anywhere, which is the species' whole biography and the reason the Vine can hand out load without keeping anybody.
appearance.build: Broad, soft and slow, carrying a winter's weight visibly across the shoulders and losing it every summer in a way that makes her look like a different woman to anyone who only sees her twice a year.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly waxy in the cold months, flushed deep in the summer, with the softness of a body that spends half the year storing and half the year spending and shows the whole of it in the face.
appearance.hair: Pale brown going grey, worn in a plain knot when she is warm and loose when she is cold, which is the only season-marker her sworn brothers use to judge her.
appearance.eyes: Pale grey and patient by physiology rather than by discipline, with the particular steadiness of a body that can be still for eight months and considers a week a short attention span.
appearance.palette: Vine brown and cold stone carry almost the whole figure, and the one saturated accent is her own heat: the picture is lit from her, faintly, so she is the only warm source in a frame full of grey. The Vine's load-marks are unbleached cord, worn at the wrist.
appearance.attire: Heavy cold-climate wool in layers, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and a broad belt she uses for the weight of whatever she has been asked to hold. Nothing she wears is a rank, because the office she holds hands out no stat to put on.
appearance.marks: A cord mark at the wrist where the Vine's load-cord has been worn, and a pale line across the shoulder from a pack-frame she has carried every summer for thirty years.
appearance.bearing: Heavy-footed and unhurried, with a slow rise and a slow fall that read as patience and are in fact a body finishing an annual cycle.

canon.role_in_story: Every sworn member of the Iron Vine who holds no office is a Ward: the unbounded office, which recognises no stat at all, because what the Vine hands out is load and not edge. Ilva is a Ward. She is the strongest thing the house can put in a place and the only thing in it that has a season, and the house has spent a hundred and eleven years finding that a body which stores its winter as fat rather than as qi can be given anything and will not stay, which is exactly what a house that gives out load wants and cannot easily admit it wants.
canon.first_appearance: First seen asleep against a load post on the ridge at the change of season, fully dressed and with her hands still hooked into a coil of cord, waking before she is touched and asking what month it is.
canon.lore: A longwinter survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle, packing a winter as body fat rather than as qi. That single decision puts the flank vessels out of reach: they need two warm gradients held at once, and a longwinter only has one, briefly, in summer. The species therefore reaches far and never stays there, which is why the setting's best long-haul traders are all cold-climate bodies, and why a house that hands out load can rely on a longwinter to carry and not to remain.
history: Born into a trading household that moved on the strength of the season, and packed her first winter as fat with no qi in it at all, which is the species' ordinary first year and the whole of its design.
Cleared the ordinary meridian set on the summer's single warm gradient and lost the flank vessels every winter for eleven years, learning that the ladder is available twice a year and gone by autumn.
Sworn to the Iron Vine at fifty-two, on the terms the Vine offers every sworn member without a stat attached: no office, no recognition, load when there is load.
Carried the ridge stores for thirty summers and was never once asked to hold them in winter, which she has come to understand is the house's only accommodation and is not one it admits to making.

Refused, at ninety-eight, a standing commission on the ridge's permanent watch, on the grounds that a sworn member who can stand a border in winter is a sworn member who has promised something her species cannot keep.

personality.summary: Enormously patient, physically warm, and privately certain that her house's gift of load is a way of not saying goodbye. She is a woman who has spent thirty summers carrying a house's ridge and has no standing, no office and no stat, and who has started describing that as a kind of honesty.
traits: can hold a position for eight months and considers a week an insufficient attention span
carries more than her share without ever being asked to and without ever being thanked in a form she could file
loses the flank vessels every winter and describes it as an arrangement rather than a failure
is the warmest body in any room and treats it as a nuisance rather than a qualification
mannerisms: asks what season it is before she asks anything else, on waking
coils cord while she talks, without noticing she has picked it up
sleeps standing against whatever is nearest and wakes before she is touched
sheds her layers in a fixed order as the season turns, and the Vine's stores are arranged around that order
motivations: wants the Vine to write down that load is what the house hands out, so that a Warden who is spent is a cost and not a matter of temperament
wants one winter to be recorded as one season of service, which the house has no field for
wants the ridge's permanent watch to be staffed by somebody who will still be standing there in February
wants to be told that refusing the commission was correct by somebody who knows what a flank vessel needs
flaws: has decided that being unpaid and unranked is a kind of honesty, and has stopped asking what it costs
is loyal to a house because it gives her load, which is the same as saying she is loyal to being useful
cannot stay in one place through a winter, so every commitment she makes has a term nobody writes down
keeps the cord marks on her wrist and describes them as belonging to the house
personality.voice: Very slow, very warm, and largely silent through the cold months. When she speaks she speaks in loads and seasons rather than in days, and she has one joke about a pack-frame that she tells once a year and gets better at.

relationships.note: Every sworn member of the Iron Vine holding no office is a Ward, and the office is unbounded and recognises no stat at all, because what the Vine hands out is load and not edge. She is the clearest instance of that arrangement the house has produced: a body strong enough to be given anything, carrying none of it past a season, and holding no claim on the house whatsoever.

That prohibition bars any teaching, text, story or practice describing the self leaving the body, on the ground that such a teaching is a promise made to people with one road, because a garrison told it can leave is a garrison that leaves. She is a Mind path sworn member of a house on a ridge, which is exactly the combination the prohibition exists to prevent, and she has never once described what she is doing as leaving.

The Vigil's god is a flock rather than a being and is kept as an itinerary rather than addressed, because elemental law is unwritten on the ridge so the pass has no season and the only schedule the frame can supply is one an animal repeats. Her hibernation is the setting's other body that runs on a schedule no office can file, and the house has never once been asked to record hers.

A trial ground is laid out on a frame that cannot say where anything is: a ring of standing markers spaced by ear and checked by sound, because possession on the plains is proven by a marker standing rather than by measuring where it stands. The Vine's claim on her is the same kind of claim in reverse — it is proven by her carrying, and stops the moment she sets it down.

An emberhollow refines faster than anything on the plains and is dead of its own cultivation at forty-five, with a ceiling of eight inherited from the ash parent and arriving earlier. The Vine gives him load too and he burns it, and the difference between them is that his spending is visible and hers is not, which is the only reason the house has never written it down.

A tidecaller is assembled for looking rather than for being hit and lives long enough to read a crossing; a longwinter is assembled for storing and goes quiet for a season. The Vine has one of each, hands both of them load, and has never worked out that the house's two most useful bodies cannot be in the same place at the same time of year.

One region carries two incompatible reckonings and which calendar a contract is written in decides whether it can be disputed at all. Hers is neither: a body that is unavailable for a third of the year and available for the rest has no calendar anybody here writes in, so every commitment she makes has a term nobody has recorded.

reference_stats.summary: Enormous carrying capacity and no way to use it twice. Everything she has is in the frame and the frame is unavailable for a third of the year, which makes her the most valuable body in any one season and the least reliable across a year.
strengths: carries more than any other sworn body in the house and carries it for months without setting it down
the body path is complete and excellent, and better after a hibernation, so a cold season is a gain rather than a loss
the mind path is open by physiology rather than by discipline, which means her patience is not something she has to maintain
cannot be frightened, hurried, or starved, and a winter costs her nothing she cannot rebuild
can hold one position so long that a garrison's term looks like a shift
weaknesses: the flank vessels need two warm gradients held at once and her species has one, briefly, in summer, so the seventeenth gate is available twice a year and lost by autumn
has no reserve worth naming and everything she has is in what she is currently holding
cannot be in one place through a winter, so every post she is offered is a post she must decline or abandon
is thirty years older than the body's best output and knows the season is going rather than the term
reference_stats.combat_read: Pick the season, not the fight. A longwinter is the strongest thing in the setting for about four months and effectively absent for eight, so an approach that arrives in autumn has already won against the setting's best carrier and has not struck anything. In summer she cannot be hurried, cannot be moved off a position and has nothing stored to spend — bring weight you can spare and be somewhere warm.
notes: The Vine quotes no stat line for her, because the office recognises no stat at all and the house has never once recorded what a Warden is worth.
The cord mark at her wrist is the only insignia the house has ever issued to her, and she describes it as belonging to the house rather than to the office.

art.palette_notes: Vine brown and cold stone carry almost the whole figure, and the picture is lit from her — a low warm bloom off her collar and her hands — so she is the only warm source in a grey frame. Cold is drawn as a rim on everything else rather than as a colour of its own. Ink contours soft and heavy through the wool, dissolving at the loosened hair, the drawing hand of somebody who works in coats.

identity.realm: Eighth gate and no further. A commonborn's ceiling is where mortals stop, and it lends no discipline at all: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so a body this even must choose one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest

appearance.presentation: A sworn member of a sect that recognises nothing, which makes her the only person at the house who is both fully entitled and entirely invisible. She reads as ordinary to a fault, and has noticed that the sect's door is the only door in the setting she can walk through without anybody deciding she is a visitor first.
appearance.age: Forty-one. A commonborn's span is a hundred years, which means she is less than halfway and in no hurry about any of it, and it also means the sect that will not recognise her has thirty or forty more years of her.
appearance.build: Ordinary, durable and slightly weathered, thick through the forearm from work rather than from any training, and standing with the settled weight of somebody who expects to be here for some time.
appearance.complexion: Plain sun-brown, weathered unevenly from the plains' outdoor season and the sect's indoor winter, with a permanent crease line across the forehead from squinting into a frame's light.
appearance.hair: Brown, cut at the jaw in the sect's fashion which is to say short and never once discussed, and tied back while she trains and loose the rest of the time.
appearance.eyes: Grey-brown and level, with a particular watchfulness in them that is the only thing about her that looks expensive.
appearance.palette: Disciple undyed wool and plain brown carry almost the entire value range, with one saturated accent she chose for herself and was not asked to justify: a narrow band of faded red at her wrist, which is not the sect's colour and which nobody in the house has ever queried.
appearance.attire: Undyed wool over plain brown, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, boots resoled twice in her life. Nothing in the clothing identifies an office, because she holds none, and the sect issues identical clothing to everyone who is sworn and nothing at all to anyone who is not.
appearance.marks: A callus ridge across both palms from the eighth gate's meridian work, and a narrow red band worn into the wrist skin at the same place every day.
appearance.bearing: Straight, unhurried and entirely without standing, which in a sect that recognises nothing is indistinguishable from enormous authority.

canon.role_in_story: The Disciple is the open door of the sect: everyone who is sworn and holds no office sits here in all but name, and it recognises nothing at all, because recognition begins where office begins. Dvine is sworn, holds no office, cultivates the body path to the gate every mortal body here reaches, and has therefore spent twenty years inside an institution whose entire content is a refusal to say anything about her, on the tier where the whole remaining ladder was shut from the inside by a frame that seats three laws and admits no humanoid.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the sect's door clearing a queue she was not on duty for, and asked by a visiting candidate whether she was teaching, and answering that the sect does not teach and she is not teaching and the door is open anyway.
canon.lore: The commonborn is the body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them. It stops where mortals stop and lends no discipline, which is exactly why it is weak: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so it has to settle on one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. Mind is closed to it outright, because a body that even has no native faculty for it. What it has instead is reach — ordinary organs, a full cavity, a channel that can be run between each pair — so the ordinary ladder is available to it as far as it goes and not one step further.
history: Born into a common household on the plains with the most ordinary concentration in the setting and no line of its own, which the household treated as reliability rather than as anything to spend.
Chose the body path at fifteen and was told, correctly, that she would be weakest exactly where a specialist was strongest, and chose it anyway because it was the only door she could see.
Cleared the ordinary meridian set by thirty and stopped, because the eighth gate is where mortals stop and no commonborn has ever been issued a ninth.

Sworn to the Disciple at twenty-one and given clothing identical to four hundred other people and no instruction of any kind, because the sect recognises nothing at all and recognition begins where office begins.

Began, without being asked and without any part of it being in the sect's remit, keeping a list of the sworn who had no office, on the grounds that a house which recognises nothing ought at least to count.

personality.summary: Competent, unresented, and privately certain that a sect's refusal to recognise her is the most honest thing anybody has ever said to her. She is a woman with no rank and a full ladder, and she has decided that being unranked in a house that hands out nothing is preferable to being ranked in one that would.

is entirely without standing in an institution whose only practice is to hand out no standing

wants the eighth gate named in the sect's own teaching, because a closed list taught as a foundation is the only curriculum the tier has
wants to be the one who says plainly that the tier licenses plants and beasts and admits no humanoid, and has been told there is no occasion

personality.voice: Plain, quick and entirely without ceremony. She names a gate before a name and a name before a feeling, and has one flat observation about the sect's open door that she has made exactly once and in public.

relationships.note: Everyone sworn and holding no office sits in all but name at the open door, and it recognises nothing at all, because recognition begins where office begins. She is the purest case the house produces: twenty years inside a full ladder with no instruction, no rank and no name on anything, in exchange for a door that is open to her and to nobody who is not.

The fourth gate asks for heart, small intestine, bladder and kidney as distinct structures with a channel between each pair, and a cairnborn's interior is one tidal cavity with nowhere to run from and nothing to close a loop against, so it never advances past the gate set. She reaches the eighth on the strength of having ordinary organs, which means the ordinary ladder is available to her body precisely because there is nothing special about it.

The mortal tier's whole curriculum is physical, life and qi, taught as a closed list rather than as a foundation, because a three-slot frame cannot carry a fourth subject. Her path is the first of the three and she has never once been taught a fourth subject, which is not a curriculum choice but a fact about the frame she lives in.

That denomination forbids teaching any of the three Daos to a child before the child can read the law census itself, and it names Body Dao first, because Body Dao's home tier licenses no humanoid so every teacher of it on the plains is a visitor collecting a gate fee. She teaches nothing, holds no office and would be the perfect reader of a census she has never been shown.

The commons of the plains is a hundred-year body with a ceiling of eight realms on a frame seating only three laws, so nobody here expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season. Her eighth gate is that ceiling, and the sect's refusal to say so out loud is the only respect anybody pays the fact.

That clan holds no plot and no office and only a numbered place in a queue for tenure, because a family with no queue slot has no claim at all and the queue cannot be shortened by anybody. She is inside a sect that declines to recognise her and came from a house that only holds a number, so she has never in her life been recognised by either.

The commonborn stops where mortals stop and lends no discipline, so it must settle on one path early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. Her whole identity is the absence of a gift, which is the only reason she is the sect's most competent unranked member and the only member nobody has asked to teach.

The lexicon distinguishes a technique failing at full strength from merely being weaker, because that is the only reading that tells a hole from a handicap. On a three-slot frame every practitioner on this tier is somewhere on that scale, and she is the only sworn member who uses the word correctly about the house she lives in.

reference_stats.summary: A full ordinary ladder and nothing at all beyond it, which makes her a genuinely competent mortal body and a dead end by anatomy. Everything she has is in the frame, the frame has no reserve worth taking, and the eighth gate is a wall rather than a schedule.
strengths: clears every ordinary meridian and holds the eighth gate, so there is no gate any ordinary body here passes that she cannot
reaches further through the meridian set than any specialist body, because the path costs her nothing that her anatomy does not already have
cannot be frightened, exhausted or confused, because there is no interior voice for any of that to happen in
costs the sect nothing: she trains, teaches nothing, is given no instruction and asks for no office
weaknesses: no gift whatsoever, so she is weakest exactly where a specialist is strongest and has known it since fifteen
the mind path is closed to her species outright, so no technique needing an interior voice can be used on her
no reserve beyond the eighth gate and no ninth has ever been issued, so there is nothing above her to aim at
no standing in the sect, no rank anywhere else, and a family holding only a queue number
reference_stats.combat_read: Fight her in the first hour. Everything she has is in the frame and the frame has no reserve, so an approach that survives her first exchange has already won the long part. The counters are a specialist body, anything needing an interior voice, and simply time — there is no realm she reaches in order to become a different fight.
notes: The sect quotes no stat line for her, because the sect recognises nothing at all and has no column for any person in it.
The list of the sworn who hold no office is the only document the house has ever produced and it is kept on the back of a training sheet.

art.palette_notes: Undyed wool and plain brown carry almost the whole figure, with one saturated accent she is not supposed to have: the narrow faded red band at her wrist. Light is drawn as ordinary interior daylight through a doorway — even, low contrast, no drama — so the red band is the only thing in the picture that anybody chose. Ink contours plain and unfussy, the drawing hand of somebody who was taught nothing and has therefore drawn it herself.

shots.pose: at the middle of the task, A sworn member of a sect that recognises nothing, which makes her the only person at the house who is both fully entitled and entirely invisible. She reads as ordinary to a fault, and has noticed that the sect's door is the only door in the setting she can walk through without anybody deciding she is a visitor first., the work proceeding whether or not it is observed
shots.expression: tired and specific, the tiredness of a repeated task rather than of age
shots.framing: waist-up at rest between tasks, hands occupied, nothing performed
